senses.title: A scientist of body functions
senses.titleCN: 研究身体机能的科学家
senses.definition: a scientist whose field is the functions of living organisms
senses.definitionCN: 以生命体机能为研究领域的科学家
senses.example: The physiologist will measure how our bodies adapt to low oxygen.
senses.exampleCN: 这位生理学家将测量我们的身体如何适应低氧。
senses.why: Physiology names the field and -ist names the person, so the word is simply the practitioner of that science.
senses.whyCN: physiology 指学科，-ist 指人，因此这个词就是该科学的从业者。

senses.title: A medical physiologist
senses.definition: a specialist who studies body functions in relation to health and disease
senses.definitionCN: 研究与健康和疾病相关的身体机能的专家
senses.example: The medical physiologist traced the hormone's effect on kidney function.
senses.exampleCN: 这位医学生理学家追踪了该激素对肾功能的影响。
senses.why: Medicine narrows the field to the functions that keep people well or make them ill.
senses.whyCN: 医学把这一领域收窄到维持健康或导致疾病的机能。

senses.title: A plant physiologist
senses.definition: a scientist who studies how plants function
senses.definitionCN: 研究植物如何运作的科学家
senses.example: The plant physiologist grafted shoots to test water uptake.
senses.exampleCN: 这位植物生理学家嫁接枝条以检验吸水情况。
senses.why: Plants pose different functional problems, so the same title takes a botanical specialism.
senses.whyCN: 植物提出不同的功能问题，因此同一头衔可带植物学专长。

senses.title: An exercise physiologist
senses.definition: a specialist in how the body responds to exercise
senses.definitionCN: 研究身体如何回应运动的专家
senses.example: The exercise physiologist designed a training plan around oxygen capacity.
senses.exampleCN: 这位运动生理学家围绕摄氧能力设计了训练计划。
senses.why: Sport turns function into performance, and a whole applied role grows around the measurement.
senses.whyCN: 运动把机能变成表现，一整个应用角色便围绕测量生长出来。

senses.title: A comparative physiologist
senses.definition: a scientist who compares functions across species
senses.definitionCN: 跨物种比较机能的科学家
senses.example: The comparative physiologist compared heat loss in desert and arctic mammals.
senses.exampleCN: 这位比较生理学家比较了沙漠与北极哺乳动物的散热。
senses.why: Comparison across species makes the physiologist an evolutionary as well as a laboratory worker.
senses.whyCN: 跨物种比较使生理学家既是实验室工作者，也是演化研究者。

senses.title: A laboratory researcher
senses.definition: a researcher who runs controlled experiments on living systems
senses.definitionCN: 对生命系统进行受控实验的研究者
senses.example: The physiologist recorded breathing rates for six hours.
senses.exampleCN: 这位生理学家记录了六小时的呼吸频率。
senses.why: The title also marks a working role: someone who instruments, records and repeats measurements.
senses.whyCN: 这个头衔也标记一种工作角色：安装仪器、记录并重复测量的人。

senses.title: A teacher of physiology
senses.definition: a person who teaches physiology to students
senses.definitionCN: 向学生讲授生理学的人
senses.example: The physiologist lectured on circulation before the practical class.
senses.exampleCN: 这位生理学家在实验课之前讲了循环系统。
senses.why: A researcher who teaches carries the same title, because the field and the classroom share one name.
senses.whyCN: 做研究又教学的人带着同一头衔，因为研究与课堂共享一个学科名。

senses.title: An author or expert consulted
senses.titleCN: 被咨询的生理学专家或作者
senses.definition: a recognized expert whose written or spoken judgement is sought
senses.definitionCN: 其书面或口头判断被求教的公认专家
senses.example: The physiologist was asked to review the safety data.
senses.exampleCN: 这位生理学家被请去审查安全数据。
senses.why: Outside the lab the title works as credentials, allowing others to rely on a judgement they cannot make themselves.
senses.whyCN: 在实验室之外，这个头衔是一种资历，使他人能依赖自己无法作出的判断。

intro.en: Physiologist is physiology plus the agent suffix -ist, which reached English through Latin and French from Greek -istēs; the whole word is a nineteenth-century formation.
intro.cn: physiologist 是 physiology 加施事后缀 -ist，该后缀经拉丁语与法语来自希腊 -istēs；整词是 19 世纪的构词。

items.en: Physis meant nature, from phyein to grow; the deeper Indo-European base is reconstructed.
items.cn: physis 意为自然，来自 phyein「生长」；更深的印欧语基属重构形式。

items.en: Physiologia joined physis to -logia, naming an inquiry into nature.
items.cn: physiologia 把 physis 与 -logia 结合，指对自然的探究。

items.en: The agent suffix -istēs marked a person who does or practises something, and it became Latin -ista and English -ist.
items.cn: 施事后缀 -istēs 标记从事或实践某活动的人，后变为拉丁 -ista 与英语 -ist。

items.en: English physiology arrived in the late sixteenth century; the personal noun followed once the field had a professional identity.
items.cn: 英语 physiology 于 16 世纪晚期进入；待该领域形成职业身份后，指人的名词随之出现。

items.en: As laboratories and medical schools expanded, physiologist separated from physician and biologist as a distinct title.
items.cn: 随着实验室与医学院扩张，physiologist 与 physician、biologist 分离，成为独立头衔。

items.en: Source uncertain only as to the first date of the English personal noun, which is usually given approximately; the roots and the suffix are well attested.
items.cn: 来源仅在人称名词的英语首见年代上不确定，通常只给约数；词根与后缀均有充分书证。

note.en: Group one holds titles and words that look almost identical to physiologist; group two holds neighbouring scientific roles.
note.cn: 第一组是几乎与 physiologist 同形的头衔与词；第二组是相邻的科学职业。

entries.definition: The science itself; the -ist form names the person who practises it.
entries.definitionCN: 这门科学本身；-ist 形式指从事它的人。

entries.definition: The adjective describing functions; it modifies nouns but does not name a person.
entries.definitionCN: 描述机能的形容词；它修饰名词，但不指人。

entries.definition: A medical doctor; the ending looks similar but the word names a clinician, not a researcher in physiology.
entries.definitionCN: 医生；词尾看似相近，但这个词指临床医生，而非生理学研究者。

entries.definition: A specialist in physics; one letter apart in speech, a different science entirely.
entries.definitionCN: 物理学专家；语音上只差一点，却是完全不同的学科。

entries.definition: A scientist of life broadly; physiology is one of the biologist's possible specialisms.
entries.definitionCN: 广义研究生命的科学家；生理学是生物学家可能选择的专长之一。

entries.definition: A specialist in body structure; the anatomist describes parts, the physiologist explains their workings.
entries.definitionCN: 身体结构的专家；解剖学家描述部件，生理学家解释其运作。

entries.definition: A scientist of the chemistry of life; much physiological work is done at this molecular level.
entries.definitionCN: 研究生命化学的科学家；许多生理学工作在这一分子层面完成。

entries.definition: A doctor who treats patients; a physiologist may advise clinicians without treating anyone.
entries.definitionCN: 诊治病人的医生；生理学家可能为临床医生提供建议，却不亲自治疗。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Physiology plus -ist: the person who practises the science of function.
normal.cn: physiology 加 -ist：实践机能科学的人。

normal.en: The title takes specialisms: exercise, plant, clinical, comparative.
normal.cn: 这个头衔可带专长：运动、植物、临床、比较。

normal.en: The family runs physiology, physiological, physiologically.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 physiology、physiological、physiologically。

normal.en: A physiologist measures; an anatomist describes; a clinician treats.
normal.cn: 生理学家测量，解剖学家描述，临床医生治疗。

normal.en: The person noun arose as laboratories created a profession.
normal.cn: 随着实验室造就一种职业，指人的名词才出现。

abstract.en: Picture a researcher standing beside a treadmill with a notebook.
abstract.cn: 想象一位研究者拿着记录本站在跑步机旁。

abstract.en: Picture a translator who turns body signals into numbers.
abstract.cn: 想象一位译者，把身体信号转成数字。

abstract.en: Picture a mechanic who studies engines without repairing them.
abstract.cn: 想象一位技师研究引擎却不修车。

examples.en: The physiologist spent the summer measuring oxygen use in migrant birds.
examples.cn: 这位生理学家整个夏天都在测量候鸟的耗氧量。

examples.en: A plant physiologist explained why the leaves closed at noon.
examples.cn: 一位植物生理学家解释了叶片为何在正午闭合。

examples.en: The committee invited a physiologist to assess the exercise protocol.
examples.cn: 委员会请了一位生理学家评估这套运动方案。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「physio 身体 + logist 研究者」——研究身体如何运作的人 → 生理学家

root: physiology + -ist（希腊 -istēs「从事者」）；physiology 源自希腊 physis「自然」+ -logia「研究」；整词为 19 世纪构词，首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the general scientist to medical, plant, exercise and comparative roles, then to the lab worker, the teacher and the consulted expert.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一般科学家走向医学、植物、运动与比较角色，再走向实验室工作者、教师与被咨询的专家。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person with a notebook beside a body in motion, turning function into recorded numbers.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人拿着记录本站在运动中的身体旁，把机能变成记录下来的数字。

branches.en: FIELD AND PERSON: the title is simply the science plus the agent suffix.
branches.cn: 学科与人：头衔就是学科加施事后缀。

branches.en: SPECIALISM: plants and athletes turn the same title into different jobs.
branches.cn: 专长：植物与运动员使同一头衔变成不同工作。

branches.en: COMPARISON AND LAB: some compare species, others record one system for hours.
branches.cn: 比较与实验室：有人比较物种，有人连续数小时记录一个系统。

branches.en: TEACHING: the researcher also stands in front of a class.
branches.cn: 教学：研究者也站在课堂前面。

branches.en: AUTHORITY: outside the lab the title lets others trust a judgement.
branches.cn: 权威：在实验室之外，头衔使他人信任某种判断。

intro.en: Physiologist is a Greek-derived field name plus a Greek-derived agent suffix, and both parts are highly productive in English.
intro.cn: physiologist 是一个希腊来源的领域名加一个希腊来源的施事后缀，两部分在英语中都高度能产。

latinIntro.en: Greek physis gives physiology; Greek -istēs, through Latin -ista, gives the person suffix seen in biologist, chemist and economist.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 physis 给出 physiology；希腊 -istēs 经拉丁 -ista 给出 biologist、chemist、economist 中可见的指人后缀。

items.example: The root survives in physics and physiology.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根存留于 physics 与 physiology 中。

items.example: The suffix turns a field into a profession.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把领域变成职业。
生理学家测量了摄氧量。
这一反应在生理上不同。

definition_zh: 钢琴；钢琴演奏；钢琴声部
definition_en: a large keyboard instrument whose strings are struck by hammers; also the skill of playing it and its part in a piece of music
core_image: 一排黑白琴键在灯下向远处延伸，琴盖被支起
scene: 琴房的门关着，木地板被午后的光照得发亮，一个孩子把手指悬在黑白琴键上方不敢落下。The piano stood open in the corner, waiting for the first note.
sceneCN: 这里 piano 指「钢琴」（第 1 个义项：那台键盘乐器）；句意为钢琴开着盖立在角落，等着第一个音。图中可辨识物件：黑白琴键、支起的琴盖、谱架。

pos.zh: 钢琴；钢琴演奏；钢琴声部

derivatives.zh: 由 piano 加 -ist 构成，义为「钢琴家」
由意大利语 piano（弱）与 forte（强）复合而成，是钢琴的旧称
由意大利语 piano 加最高级词尾 -issimo 构成，义为「极弱地」

senses.title: The keyboard instrument
senses.definition: a large musical instrument with a row of black and white keys that send hammers to strike strings inside a wooden case
senses.definitionCN: 一种大型乐器，黑白琴键带动木箱内的琴槌敲击琴弦发声
senses.example: The piano stood open in the corner of the room.
senses.exampleCN: 钢琴开着盖立在房间角落。
senses.why: Italian piano meant soft, and the instrument's full name pianoforte said it could sound both soft and strong, which was exactly what the older harpsichord could not do.
senses.whyCN: 意大利语 piano 意为轻柔，这件乐器的全名 pianoforte 是在说它既能弱也能强，而这正是旧式羽管键琴做不到的事。

senses.title: The skill or subject of playing it
senses.definition: the art or school subject of playing this instrument, as in studying piano at a conservatory
senses.definitionCN: 演奏这件乐器的技艺或学校科目，如音乐学院里的钢琴专业
senses.example: He studied piano for ten years before he ever performed in public.
senses.exampleCN: 他学了十年钢琴才第一次公开演出。
senses.why: English lets the name of an instrument stand for the skill practised on it, so piano becomes a subject you can study, teach, or take an exam in.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许乐器名直接指在这件乐器上练出来的技艺，于是 piano 成了一门可以学、可以教、可以考试的科目。

senses.title: The piano part in a score or ensemble
senses.definition: the line or part written for the piano in a score, especially when it plays alongside other instruments
senses.definitionCN: 总谱中写给钢琴的那一行或那一声部，尤指与其他乐器合奏时
senses.example: The piano enters softly under the strings in the second movement.
senses.exampleCN: 第二乐章里，钢琴在弦乐之下轻轻进入。
senses.why: Once a score lists instruments by name, each named staff can be called by its instrument, so the piano printed on the page becomes the piano heard in the hall.
senses.whyCN: 总谱一旦按乐器名称分列各行，每一行就能直接用乐器名来称呼，于是印在纸上的「钢琴」变成了大厅里听到的钢琴声部。

intro.en: Piano is a shortened Italian phrase: the full name of the instrument described its ability to sound soft as well as loud.
intro.cn: piano 是意大利语短语的缩略：这件乐器的全名描述的是它既能弱也能强。

items.en: Planus meant flat, level, or plain, and it is the distant source of the Italian word for soft and smooth.
items.cn: planus 意为平的、平坦的、平实的，是意大利语中表示柔和、平滑那个词的远源。

items.en: Italian piano meant soft or smooth, and musicians used it as a direction to play quietly.
items.cn: 意大利语 piano 意为轻柔、平滑，乐师用它作「轻声演奏」的指示。

items.en: Pianoforte joined piano, soft, with forte, strong, to name a harpsichord-like instrument that could do both.
items.cn: pianoforte 把表示「弱」的 piano 与表示「强」的 forte 拼在一起，用来命名一种既能弱又能强、类似羽管键琴的乐器。

items.en: English borrowed the instrument and shortened the long name to piano, which then became the everyday word.
items.cn: 英语借来这件乐器，并把长名缩短为 piano，随后它成了日常说法。

items.en: Modern English uses piano for the instrument, for the skill, and for the part, while the full name survives mostly in formal writing.
items.cn: 现代英语用 piano 指乐器、技艺与声部，而旧的全名大多只留在正式文字里。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Italian word and the forms built on it; the near-meaning group gathers other keyboard instruments.
note.cn: 形近组沿着这个意大利语词及其派生形式排列；近义组收其他键盘乐器。

entries.definition: A person who plays the piano, often as a profession.
entries.definitionCN: 弹钢琴的人，常指职业钢琴家。

entries.definition: The full eighteenth-century name of the instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 这件乐器在十八世纪的全名。

entries.definition: A musical direction meaning very soft.
entries.definitionCN: 音乐术语：极弱地。

entries.definition: The art or technique of piano playing.
entries.definitionCN: 钢琴演奏的艺术或技巧。

entries.definition: A large keyboard instrument that makes sound by driving air through pipes.
entries.definitionCN: 靠气流通过音管发声的大型键盘乐器；管风琴。

entries.definition: An older keyboard instrument whose strings are plucked rather than struck.
entries.definitionCN: 更早的键盘乐器，琴弦被拨动而非被敲击；羽管键琴。

entries.definition: A row of keys on an instrument, or an electronic instrument built around such keys.
entries.definitionCN: 乐器上的一排琴键，或围绕琴键制成的电子乐器。

normalIntro.en: The word began life as an Italian direction for soft playing, and the instrument took that word as its name.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词原本是意大利语里「轻声演奏」的指示，乐器后来把这个词当成了自己的名字。

normal.en: Piano in Italian means soft, so the marking piano on a score still tells a player to play quietly.
normal.cn: 意大利语 piano 意为轻柔，所以谱面上的 piano 记号至今仍在告诉演奏者放轻。

normal.en: The full name pianoforte joined soft and strong, because this instrument could change volume in a way the harpsichord could not.
normal.cn: 全名 pianoforte 把「弱」与「强」拼在一起，因为这件乐器能改变音量，而羽管键琴不能。

normal.en: English cut the long name down to piano, and the short form is now the ordinary word in every shop that sells one.
normal.cn: 英语把长名砍成 piano，这个短形式如今成了每家琴行里的日常说法。

normal.en: Pianist adds -ist to piano, and the stress moves to the first syllable even though the spelling keeps the o.
normal.cn: pianist 在 piano 后加 -ist，重音移到第一个音节，但拼写里仍留着那个 o。

normal.en: The plural is pianos, not pianoes, because the word came from Italian and simply takes an s.
normal.cn: 复数是 pianos 而不是 pianoes，因为这个词来自意大利语，直接加 s。

abstract.en: A word meaning soft became the name of an instrument that can be very loud, because its novelty was the power to be quiet.
abstract.cn: 一个意为「轻柔」的词，成了一台能很响的乐器的名字，因为它的新鲜处正在于能安静下来。

abstract.en: Eighty-eight keys, one short word: the name grew shorter as the instrument grew common.
abstract.cn: 八十八个琴键，一个短词：乐器越普及，名字就越短。

abstract.en: The same word names the object, the skill and the line in the score, since all three begin at one keyboard.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指那件东西，也指那门技艺和谱面上的那一行，因为三者都从同一排琴键开始。

examples.en: The piano stood open in the corner of the room.
examples.cn: 钢琴开着盖立在房间角落。

examples.en: She has her piano lesson every Thursday afternoon.
examples.cn: 她每周四下午上钢琴课。

examples.en: The piano enters softly under the strings.
examples.cn: 钢琴在弦乐之下轻轻进入。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮阿诺」——琴键一按，声音轻得像耳语，piano 本来正是「轻柔」的意思。

root: 意大利语 piano（轻柔、平滑）源自拉丁语 planus（平的、平实的）；pianoforte 由 piano 与 forte（强）合成，英语缩略为 piano。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the instrument that can be soft and strong; from the object come the skill practised on it and the part it plays in a score.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是那件能弱能强的键盘乐器；由这件实物分出在它上面练成的技艺，以及它在总谱里担任的声部。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: black and white keys running away under a lamp, the lid propped open.
core.cn: 核心意象：灯下一排黑白琴键向远处延伸，琴盖被支起。

branches.en: a wooden case with its lid propped open
branches.cn: 琴盖支起的木制琴箱

branches.en: a child's hand hovering above the keys before the first lesson
branches.cn: 第一堂课之前悬在琴键上方的小手

branches.en: a practice room heard through a closed door
branches.cn: 隔着关着的门听见的练琴声

branches.en: a page where the piano line waits under the violins
branches.cn: 谱面上等在提琴声部下方的钢琴行

branches.en: a trio playing with one player at the keyboard
branches.cn: 三人合奏，其中一人在键盘前

intro.en: A Latin adjective for flat lies behind the Italian word for soft, and the instrument's double name was later cut in half.
intro.cn: 拉丁语中表示「平」的形容词是意大利语「轻柔」一词的来源，而乐器的双名后来被砍掉了一半。

latinIntro.en: Italian piano goes back to Latin planus, flat or plain, so the Latin entry belongs to the same family.
latinIntro.cn: 意大利语 piano 可追到拉丁语 planus（平的、平实的），所以这条拉丁词与它同属一族。

items.meaningCN: 意大利语最高级词尾：极

definition_zh: 药丸；药片；口服避孕药；不得不咽下的苦事
definition_en: a small round solid piece of medicine swallowed whole, also the daily contraceptive tablet and, figuratively, an unpleasant thing that has to be accepted
core_image: 一粒裹着糖衣的小圆药丸，静静躺在一只摊开的手心里
scene: 深夜的宿舍里，桌上摊着几板感冒药，搪瓷杯里的水还冒着热气。He shook one pill into his palm and swallowed it with a gulp of water.
sceneCN: 这里的 pill 是「药丸、药片」（第 1 个义项：整粒吞服的固体药）；句意是他抖出一粒药丸放在手心，就着一大口水咽下去。图中可辨识物件：药板、搪瓷杯、台灯。

collocations.zh: 把难接受的事说得顺耳些

derivatives.zh: 由 pill 与 box 复合而成，义为「药盒」
由 pill 与 bottle 复合而成，义为「药瓶」

senses.title: A small solid dose of medicine
senses.definition: a small round or oval piece of medicine that is swallowed whole with water
senses.definitionCN: 用水整粒吞下的小圆或椭圆形药物
senses.example: Take one pill with water after breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 早饭后用水送服一粒药。
senses.why: Latin pilula meant a little ball, because early pharmacists rolled each dose by hand into a round pellet, and that shape became the name.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pilula 本义是「小球」，因为早期药剂师把每一剂药用手搓成圆粒，这个形状后来就成了名字。

senses.title: The daily contraceptive tablet
senses.definition: the contraceptive pill taken once a day, usually referred to with the definite article
senses.definitionCN: 每天服用一次的避孕药，通常与定冠词连用
senses.example: She has been on the pill since college.
senses.exampleCN: 她从大学起就一直在服用口服避孕药。
senses.why: Because the contraceptive is taken every day and is the pill most often meant in conversation, the fixed phrase the pill narrowed to it alone.
senses.whyCN: 因为避孕药需要每天服用，也是日常对话里最常提到的那种药，固定说法 the pill 便单独指向了它。

senses.title: Something humiliating that must be accepted
senses.titleCN: 苦果；不得不忍受的难堪
senses.definition: an unpleasant fact, defeat or insult that one has no choice but to accept
senses.definitionCN: 不得不接受的不快事实、失败或羞辱
senses.example: Losing the final was a bitter pill for the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 输掉决赛对整支队伍来说是一枚难咽的苦果。
senses.why: A pill that tastes bitter still has to be swallowed for the sake of the cure, so the image of forced medicine became a metaphor for forced humiliation.
senses.whyCN: 再苦的药丸也得为了治病咽下去，于是「被迫吃药」的画面就变成了「被迫受辱」的比喻。

intro.en: Pill traces back to a Latin word for a little ball, since early doses were rolled by hand; English most likely took the word from Dutch rather than straight from Latin.
intro.cn: pill 可追到拉丁语中表示「小球」的词，因为早期药丸是手工搓成的；英语多半是从荷兰语而非直接从拉丁语借入。

items.en: Pila named a ball or any round object, and it sits at the base of the whole family.
items.cn: pila 指球或任何圆形物体，是这一族词共同的底座。

items.en: The suffix -ula shrank pila into pilula, a little ball, the word used for a rounded dose of medicine.
items.cn: 后缀 -ula 把 pila 缩小成 pilula，即「小球」，用来指搓圆的药剂。

items.en: Middle Dutch pille named a small round medicine; most dictionaries hold that English borrowed the word from here or from a very close form.
items.cn: 中古荷兰语 pille 指圆形小药丸；多数词典认为英语是从这里或与之极接近的形式借入的。

items.en: Middle English pille covered any small ball of medicine, whether chewed, swallowed or dissolved in liquid.
items.cn: 中古英语 pille 泛指各种小药丸，无论嚼服、吞服还是化在水里。

items.en: Modern English cut the word down to pill and let it cover the contraceptive and, in a bitter pill, any humiliation that has to be endured.
items.cn: 现代英语把词缩为 pill，并让它兼指避孕药，以及在 a bitter pill 中任何必须忍受的难堪。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that merely share letters with pill; the near-meaning group gathers other names for a measured dose of medicine.
note.cn: 形近组收只是与 pill 拼写相近的词；近义组收其他表示一剂药的词。

entries.definition: A heap of things lying one on another; it only looks like pill in spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 一堆叠放的东西；只是拼写和 pill 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A cushion for the head; it shares the first letters but comes from a different Latin word.
entries.definitionCN: 睡觉垫头的软垫；只是开头字母相同，来自另一个拉丁词。

entries.definition: To strip off an outer layer, or the skin of a fruit.
entries.definitionCN: 剥去外层，或指果皮。

entries.definition: A small flat round dose of medicine, usually pressed rather than rolled.
entries.definitionCN: 压制成的小圆片药，多由压制而非搓成。

entries.definition: A dose of medicine enclosed in a soluble shell.
entries.definitionCN: 装在可溶外壳里的一剂药。

entries.definition: The measured amount of a medicine taken at one time.
entries.definitionCN: 一次服用的药量。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin ball shrunk by a suffix, and the family keeps that shape: something small, round and easy to swallow.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「球」被后缀缩小的结果，同族词也保留着这个形状：小而圆、容易吞下。

normal.en: Pill starts as Latin pila, a ball, and pilula is simply a little ball; a pill is medicine rolled into that shape.
normal.cn: pill 源自拉丁语 pila（球），pilula 就是「小球」，药丸正是被搓成这个形状的药。

normal.en: The suffix -ula marks something smaller, so pilula is a pila shrunk down, which is exactly what one dose is.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ula 表示更小，pilula 就是缩小版的 pila，正好对应一剂的量。

normal.en: Sleeping pill and pain pill put the purpose in front of the word, the usual English way of building compounds.
normal.cn: sleeping pill 与 pain pill 把用途放在词前，这是英语构成复合词的常见方式。

normal.en: On the pill is a fixed phrase for the contraceptive, and the definite article does the narrowing.
normal.cn: on the pill 是口服避孕药的固定说法，定冠词完成了这层收窄。

normal.en: A bitter pill to swallow keeps the taste of medicine inside a metaphor about humiliation.
normal.cn: a bitter pill to swallow 把药的味道留在了关于难堪的比喻里。

abstract.en: A medicine small enough to swallow whole is a neat picture of anything you must simply get down.
abstract.cn: 一粒小到能整颗吞下的药，正好比喻那些只能硬着头皮接受的事。

abstract.en: One word for a cure and for a humiliation shows how close relief and endurance can sit.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指解药又指难堪，说明缓解与忍耐往往只隔一层。

abstract.en: A daily pill turns a decision into a habit, and language quietly follows the habit.
abstract.cn: 每天一粒药把决定变成习惯，语言也随之悄悄跟上了这个习惯。

examples.en: Take one pill with water after breakfast.
examples.cn: 早饭后用水送服一粒药。

examples.en: She has been on the pill since college.
examples.cn: 她从大学起就一直在服用口服避孕药。

examples.en: Losing the final was a bitter pill for the whole team.
examples.cn: 输掉决赛对整支队伍来说是一枚难咽的苦果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「皮儿」——小药丸外面总裹着一层糖皮儿，念起来就是 pill。

root: 拉丁语 pila（球）加指小后缀 -ula 得 pilula（小丸），一般认为经中古荷兰语 pille 进入英语，义为「小圆药丸」。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a round medicine; from there the word narrows to the contraceptive and widens again into a metaphor for what must be endured.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是圆形的药；由此收窄指避孕药，又向外扩展成「必须忍受之事」的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small sugar-coated ball of medicine resting in an open palm.
core.cn: 核心意象：一粒裹着糖衣的小药丸躺在摊开的手心里。

branches.en: a round pellet rolled between thumb and forefinger
branches.cn: 拇指与食指之间搓成的小圆丸

branches.en: a hand tipping one dose into an open palm
branches.cn: 掌心接住一粒倒出来的药

branches.en: a blister pack on a bathroom shelf, one dose taken each night
branches.cn: 浴室架上的药板，每晚取走一粒

branches.en: a cup of water raised to get something bitter down
branches.cn: 端起水杯把苦的东西咽下去

branches.en: a daily habit that is also a decision
branches.cn: 既是每日习惯，也是一个决定

intro.en: The word is held together by a Latin noun for a ball, a Latin suffix that makes it small, and the Dutch and English forms that turned a pellet into a tablet.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「球」的拉丁名词、把它变小的拉丁后缀，以及把药丸变成药片的荷兰语与英语形式共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Latin gave the word its ball-shaped base and the suffix that shrank it, and those two forms are the true relatives of pill.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语给了这个词「球」的底座和把它缩小的后缀，这两个形式才是 pill 真正的同族词。

definition_zh: 柱子；支柱；栋梁；柱状物；桥墩；门柱
definition_en: a tall upright support of any shape, or a person or thing regarded as essential to a group or system
core_image: 一根方正的立柱顶住门廊，旁边一根圆柱只作装饰；同一词也指撑起整座建筑的那个人
scene: 门廊左侧的方柱已被风雨磨圆了棱角。The central pillar takes most of the roof's weight, while the others only frame the entrance.
sceneCN: 这里 pillar 指「建筑中直立的支撑柱」（第 1 个义项：柱子、支柱）；句意为中央那根柱子承担屋顶的大部分重量，其余只用来框住入口。图中可辨识物件：门廊、方柱、圆柱、屋顶；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 有柱子的
（英）邮筒
柱状的
社会栋梁
支柱产业

senses.title: An upright architectural support
senses.definition: a tall upright support, square or round, often ornamental as well as structural
senses.definitionCN: 高而直立的支撑件，方或圆，常兼具装饰与承重作用
senses.example: A square pillar flanked each side of the porch.
senses.exampleCN: 门廊两侧各立一根方柱。
senses.why: the Latin source meant a pillar of any section, so the word never required the roundness of a classical column.
senses.whyCN: 其拉丁来源指任意截面的柱子，因此这个词从不要求古典柱那样的圆形。

senses.title: A person who holds up a community
senses.definition: a person regarded as a main support of a community or institution
senses.definitionCN: 被视为社区或机构主要支撑的人
senses.example: The old teacher was a pillar of the village for fifty years.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老教师五十年来一直是村里的栋梁。
senses.why: the metaphor is structural and moral at once: remove the person and the group sags.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻同时是结构与道德的：去掉这个人，群体就会塌下去。

senses.title: An essential part of a system
senses.definition: a component on which a system depends, such as a sector of an economy
senses.definitionCN: 某个系统所依赖的组成部分，如经济中的某个部门
senses.example: Tourism is a pillar of the island's income.
senses.exampleCN: 旅游业是这座岛屿收入的支柱。
senses.why: systems are described as buildings, so their load-bearing parts are described as pillars.
senses.whyCN: 系统被描述为建筑，因此其承重部分被说成柱子。

senses.title: A tall narrow mass
senses.definition: a tall narrow shape of smoke, light, salt or rock
senses.definitionCN: 烟、光、盐或岩石形成的细高形状
senses.example: A pillar of salt stood where the tide had cut the cliff.
senses.exampleCN: 潮水切开的崖边立着一根盐柱。
senses.why: the shape is enough: the word needs no load and no building.
senses.whyCN: 形状就够了：这个词不需要荷载，也不需要建筑。

senses.title: A bridge pier
senses.definition: the vertical support that carries a bridge span
senses.definitionCN: 承托桥梁跨度的竖向支撑
senses.example: The middle pillar of the bridge has been rebuilt twice.
senses.exampleCN: 桥的中墩已重建过两次。
senses.why: engineering uses the plain word for any vertical load path, not only for ornamental shafts.
senses.whyCN: 工程用这个朴素词指任何竖向承重路径，而不只用于装饰柱。

senses.title: A gatepost
senses.definition: a short sturdy post marking or carrying a gate or boundary
senses.definitionCN: 标记或承托门与边界的短粗立柱
senses.example: The gate hangs between two brick pillars.
senses.exampleCN: 大门挂在两根砖柱之间。
senses.why: one of the oldest uses is simply a post that marks a threshold.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的用法之一就是标记门槛的一根柱子。

senses.title: One of three policy supports
senses.definition: in policy language, one of several coordinated supports of a system, as in pension pillars
senses.definitionCN: 政策语言中某个体系的几根协同支柱之一，如养老金三支柱
senses.example: The report describes the three pillars of the pension scheme.
senses.exampleCN: 报告描述该养老金方案的三根支柱。
senses.why: policy analysts borrowed the architectural image to show that the system fails if one support is removed.
senses.whyCN: 政策分析者借用建筑意象，说明抽掉一根支柱体系就会失效。

senses.title: A pillar industry
senses.definition: a sector that carries a large share of a region's output and employment
senses.definitionCN: 承担某地区大部分产出与就业的产业部门
senses.example: Shipbuilding became the pillar of the coastal economy.
senses.exampleCN: 造船业成为沿海经济的支柱。
senses.why: the fixed phrase turns the metaphor into an economic category with measurable weight.
senses.whyCN: 这一固定说法把比喻变成一个有可测分量的经济范畴。

intro.en: Pillar comes from a Latin word for a pillar through Old French, and it has always meant a support of any shape. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: pillar 经古法语来自拉丁语中表示「柱子」的词，历来指任意形状的支撑。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pila named a pillar or pier; it is written the same as the word for a ball, and the two are usually treated as separate nouns.
items.cn: pila 指柱子或墩柱；它与表示「球」的词拼写相同，通常被视为两个不同的名词。

items.en: A derived noun pilare named a pillar or a supporting post in later Latin.
items.cn: 后期拉丁语中派生名词 pilare 指柱子或支撑柱。

items.en: Old French pilier carried the word into English, where it named a support in a building or a gate.
items.cn: 古法语 pilier 把这个词带入英语，指建筑或大门中的支撑。

items.en: By the medieval period the word covered bridge piers and gateposts as well as interior shafts.
items.cn: 到中世纪，这个词除室内柱身外还涵盖桥墩与门柱。

items.en: From the sixteenth century a trusted person could be called a pillar of the community or of the church.
items.cn: 从十六世纪起，受信赖的人可被称为社区或教会的栋梁。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the ancestry of pila before Latin is not established, and whether it is connected to the ball word is disputed; no shared origin has been demonstrated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深来源）：pila 在拉丁语之前的谱系未得到证明，它与表示「球」的词是否有联系也有争议；尚无证据显示两者同源。

note.en: Group one holds upright-support words that overlap with pillar; group two holds metaphorical supports and tall masses.
note.cn: 第一组是与 pillar 重叠的直立支撑词；第二组是比喻性支撑与高柱体。

entries.definition: A support, usually round and governed by an order; a pillar may be square and need follow no order.
entries.definitionCN: 通常为圆形且受柱式规范的支撑；pillar 可为方形、无须遵循柱式。

entries.definition: A thick masonry support between openings or under a bridge; it is heavier and more wall-like than a pillar.
entries.definitionCN: 开口之间或桥下的厚砌体支撑；比 pillar 更厚重、更像墙。

entries.definition: A plain upright piece of timber or metal; pillar sounds more monumental and more permanent.
entries.definitionCN: 朴素木制或金属直立件；pillar 听起来更宏大、更持久。

entries.definition: A small pillar; the suffix makes it a minor architectural member.
entries.definitionCN: 小柱子；后缀使它成为次要建筑构件。

entries.definition: The chief support of a system, from a sailing term for the rope holding a mast; it is closer to pillar sense two.
entries.definitionCN: 体系的主要支撑，来自固定桅杆的航海术语；更接近 pillar 的第二个义项。

entries.definition: A support placed under something to hold it up; it is usually temporary and rarely ornamental.
entries.definitionCN: 置于某物下方以托住的支撑，通常临时且少装饰。

entries.definition: Anything that holds weight or sustains a system; it is the neutral term that pillar makes concrete.
entries.definitionCN: 任何承重或维持体系之物；是中性的总称，pillar 使之具体化。

entries.definition: The central strength of a group or system, from the spine; it stresses unity rather than vertical support.
entries.definitionCN: 群体或体系的核心力量，来自脊柱；强调统一性而非竖向支撑。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin source, the real bridge and gate uses, and the real policy phrase.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁来源、真实的桥梁与门柱用法、真实的政策说法。

normal.en: The word never required a round shaft, so a square gatepost is as much a pillar as a marble column.
normal.cn: 这个词从不要求圆形柱身，因此方形门柱与大理石圆柱一样是 pillar。

normal.en: The family runs pillar, pillared, pillaret, pillar-box, pillar-like.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 pillar、pillared、pillaret、pillar-box、pillar-like。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the branches: stone pillar, pillar of society, bridge pillar, pillar industry.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各分支：石柱、社会栋梁、桥墩、支柱产业。

normal.en: The metaphor is load-bearing: take the person away and the group sags.
normal.cn: 这个比喻是承重的：把人抽走，群体就会塌。

normal.en: A pillar of salt and a pillar of smoke need no building at all.
normal.cn: 盐柱与烟柱根本不需要建筑。

abstract.en: Picture a village where one person is literally holding up the roof.
abstract.cn: 想象一个村庄里真有一个人托着屋顶。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge standing on one leg in the middle of a river.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥用一条腿立在河心。

abstract.en: Picture a policy report drawn as a temple with three columns.
abstract.cn: 想象一份政策报告被画成一座有三根柱子的神庙。

examples.en: The pillar at the gate carries the date of the first owner.
examples.cn: 门柱上刻着第一任主人的日期。

examples.en: She was a pillar of the hospital's volunteer service.
examples.cn: 她是这家医院志愿服务的栋梁。

examples.en: A pillar of cloud rose over the burning refinery.
examples.cn: 燃烧的炼油厂上方升起一根烟柱。

dict_mnemonic.text: pila（柱子）+ 英语名词尾 → 直立的支撑 → 柱子、支柱、栋梁

root: 古法语 pilier 来自中世纪拉丁 pilare，其源头是拉丁 pila「柱子、墩柱」；英语 pillar。pila 的更早谱系不确定，与表示「球」的 pila 是否有关尚无证据。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one upright piece: a building support becomes a person, a system part, a tall mass, a bridge pier, a gatepost, a policy support and an industry.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一根直立件展开：建筑支撑成为人、体系部件、高柱体、桥墩、门柱、政策支柱与产业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plain upright block that holds something heavier than itself.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块朴素的直立体，托着比它更重的东西。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL SUPPORT: a shaft, a pier and a gatepost are the same block in three positions.
branches.cn: 实体支撑：柱身、桥墩与门柱，是同一块直立体在三个位置。

branches.en: THE PERSON: a trusted member is described as holding the group up.
branches.cn: 人：受信赖的成员被描述为托住群体的人。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: economic sectors and policy supports are load-bearing parts.
branches.cn: 体系：经济部门与政策支撑都是承重部件。

branches.en: THE MASS: smoke, salt and light keep only the tall narrow shape.
branches.cn: 体量：烟、盐与光只保留了细高的形状。

branches.en: THE CATEGORY: the metaphor hardens into the fixed term pillar industry.
branches.cn: 范畴：比喻固化为「支柱产业」这一固定术语。

intro.en: Pillar is a borrowed noun with almost no productive affix of its own; its family is built with English endings and fixed compounds.
intro.cn: pillar 是借入名词，本身几乎没有能产词缀；其词族由英语词尾与固定复合词构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin pila and the later pilare are the direct sources; English formed pillared and pillaret from the noun, not from new Latin words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pila 与后期的 pilare 是直接来源；英语的 pillared 与 pillaret 是从名词构成，而非新的拉丁词。

items.example: Pilare named the pier of a bridge.
A stone pilier framed the gate.
A pillared porch marks the entrance.
items.exampleCN: 一道有柱的门廊标出入口。

items.example: The red pillar-box stands at the corner.

items.meaning: a sector that carries an economy
items.example: Steel was once a pillar industry here.
items.exampleCN: 钢铁一度是这里的支柱产业。

latinEntries.structure: pilare, pilaris (n., third declension; medieval Latin)

definition_zh: 飞行员；引水员；驾驶；引导；试验性的
definition_en: a person who flies an aircraft or guides a ship into harbour, the act of steering or guiding something, and a small trial version launched before the full thing
core_image: 驾驶舱里一只手握住操纵杆，前方跑道在雨雾里亮起一排灯
scene: 清晨的机场笼着薄雾，登机梯旁站着一个穿深色制服的人。The pilot walked slowly around the wing and checked it before boarding.
sceneCN: 这里的 pilot 是「飞行员」（第 1 个义项：驾驶飞机的人）；句意是飞行员绕着机翼慢慢走了一圈，登机前做了检查。图中可辨识物件：登机梯、机翼、跑道灯。

derivatives.zh: 由 pilot 加名词后缀 -age 构成，义为「引航；引航费」
由 pilot 加否定后缀 -less 构成，义为「无人驾驶的」
由 pilot 与 house 复合而成，义为「驾驶室」

senses.title: A person who flies an aircraft
senses.definition: a person trained and licensed to fly an aeroplane or other aircraft
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练并取得执照、驾驶飞机的人
senses.example: The pilot warned the passengers about the turbulence ahead.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员提醒乘客前方有气流颠簸。
senses.why: The word first named the person who steers a ship; when machines took to the air, the same steering role handed the title to the flyer.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最早指掌舵行船的人；当机器飞上天空，同一个「掌舵」的角色把称号交给了驾驶飞机的人。

senses.title: A specialist who guides a ship in harbour
senses.definition: a local expert who comes aboard to steer a ship through a harbour or a difficult channel
senses.definitionCN: 登船引导船只通过港口或复杂航道的当地专家
senses.example: A local pilot came aboard to take the ship through the narrow channel.
senses.exampleCN: 一名当地引水员登船，带这艘船穿过狭窄航道。
senses.why: In a harbour the captain hands over control to someone who knows every sandbank, so the oldest sense of a hired guide at the helm survives intact.
senses.whyCN: 在港口，船长会把控制权交给熟悉每一处沙洲的人，于是「受雇掌舵的向导」这个最古老的义项完整地留了下来。

senses.title: To steer or guide something
senses.definition: to steer an aircraft, boat or vehicle, or to guide a process through its early stages
senses.definitionCN: 操纵飞机、船只或车辆，或引导某个过程走过最初阶段
senses.example: She piloted the boat through the gap in the reef.
senses.exampleCN: 她驾着小船穿过礁石间的缺口。
senses.why: English turns a role into a verb very readily, so whoever is the pilot simply does the piloting.
senses.whyCN: 英语很习惯把角色直接变成动词，所以当 pilot 的人做的事就叫 pilot。

senses.title: Done as a trial before a full launch
senses.definition: made or done on a small scale first, in order to test whether a full version will work
senses.definitionCN: 先小规模做出或进行，用来检验完整版本是否可行
senses.example: The company ran a pilot scheme in three cities.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司在三座城市试行了一个方案。
senses.why: A pilot boat goes out ahead of the fleet to test the water, so the first small version of a project borrowed the same name.
senses.whyCN: 引水船会先于船队出海探路，于是项目最初的小规模版本也借用了这个名字。

intro.en: Pilot came into English from the sea, through French and Italian, and its medieval Latin form is the first clearly recorded one; the step before that is disputed.
intro.cn: pilot 从海上经法语和意大利语进入英语，中世纪拉丁语形式是最早清楚可考的形态；再往前的一步则有争议。

items.en: One old suggestion traces the word to Greek pedon, an oar; the link is attractive but has never been proved, so it is best marked as uncertain.
items.cn: 一种旧说法把这个词追到希腊语 pedon（桨）；这条线索很吸引人，但从未得到证实，最好标为不确定。

items.en: Medieval Latin pilotus named the man who steers a ship, and it is the earliest form that can be quoted with confidence.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 pilotus 指掌舵行船的人，是能够有把握引用的最早形态。

items.en: Italian pilota carried the nautical sense across Mediterranean trade routes.
items.cn: 意大利语 pilota 沿地中海贸易路线传播了这个航海义。

items.en: Middle French pilot brought the word into English in the fifteenth century, still tied to ships and harbours.
items.cn: 中古法语 pilot 在十五世纪把这个词带进英语，当时仍与船和港口绑定。

items.en: Modern English moved the word from harbour to airfield, then to any small trial that goes first.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词从港口搬到了机场，再延伸到任何先走一步的小规模试验。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that merely resemble pilot in spelling; the near-meaning group collects other people who steer or find the way.
note.cn: 形近组收只是拼写与 pilot 相似的词；近义组收其他掌舵或寻路的人。

entries.definition: The central point on which something turns; the spelling is close but the source is different.
entries.definitionCN: 物体转动的中心点；拼写接近，来源不同。

entries.definition: A tall tower that carries cables or marks a route.
entries.definitionCN: 架线或标示路线的高塔。

entries.definition: A person who travels a long way to a holy place.
entries.definitionCN: 长途前往圣地的人。

entries.definition: A person who flies aircraft, an older and more formal word.
entries.definitionCN: 驾驶飞机的人，较旧、较正式的说法。

entries.definition: The crew member who works out the route.
entries.definitionCN: 负责计算航线的机组人员。

entries.definition: The person who steers a ship.
entries.definitionCN: 掌舵行船的人。

normalIntro.en: The word is a steering role that has changed element twice, from water to air to the early stage of a project.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个掌舵的角色，换过两次场域：从水上到空中，再到项目的最初阶段。

normal.en: Pilot began at sea: it named the man who steered a ship long before anyone flew.
normal.cn: pilot 起于海上：早在有人飞行之前，它就指掌舵行船的人。

normal.en: Pilotage adds -age to name the work and the fee, the same suffix as in postage.
normal.cn: pilotage 加 -age 表示这份工作和费用，和 postage 用的是同一个后缀。

normal.en: Pilotless adds -less, so a pilotless aircraft is one without the person the word first named.
normal.cn: pilotless 加 -less，所以无人驾驶的飞机就是少了这个词最初指的那个人。

normal.en: Pilot project puts the noun in front as a modifier, and that modifier says the project goes first.
normal.cn: pilot project 把名词放在前面作修饰，这个修饰语说明项目要先走一步。

normal.en: Harbour pilot and airline pilot show the same role in two elements, water and air.
normal.cn: harbour pilot 与 airline pilot 展示了同一个角色在水与空两个场域里的样子。

abstract.en: To pilot something new is to go ahead of everyone else and find the rocks first.
abstract.cn: 试行一件新事，就是走在所有人前面，先摸到暗礁。

abstract.en: The same word covers a ship, a plane and a trial, because all three need someone at the front.
abstract.cn: 同一个词兼指船、飞机和试验，因为三者都需要有人在最前面。

abstract.en: A pilot project is small on purpose, a way of testing the water before the whole fleet sails.
abstract.cn: 试点项目故意做得小，是在整支船队出发前先试试水深。

examples.en: The pilot warned the passengers about the turbulence ahead.
examples.cn: 飞行员提醒乘客前方有气流颠簸。

examples.en: She piloted the boat through the gap in the reef.
examples.cn: 她驾着小船穿过礁石间的缺口。

examples.en: The company ran a pilot scheme in three cities.
examples.cn: 这家公司在三座城市试行了一个方案。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「派了他」——机长派了他去驾驶飞机，他就是 pilot。

root: 中世纪拉丁语 pilotus（掌舵者）经意大利语 pilota、中古法语 pilot 进入英语；更早的来源一般认为与希腊语 pedon（桨）有关，但不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the person who steers; the senses then move from harbour to aircraft, from the role to the action, and finally to anything that goes first as a trial.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是掌舵的人；义项由此从港口转到飞机，从角色转到动作，最后转到任何先行试探的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand on the control column while runway lights slide past in the rain.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手握住操纵杆，跑道灯在雨中向后退去。

branches.en: a small boat coming out to meet a ship at the harbour mouth
branches.cn: 港口外一条小船驶向大船

branches.en: a hand on the yoke while the runway lights slide past
branches.cn: 手握操纵杆，跑道灯向后退去

branches.en: a crew walking round the wing in the cold morning air
branches.cn: 机组在清冷的晨风里绕机翼检查

branches.en: a project tested in three towns before a national launch
branches.cn: 项目先在三座城市试运行

branches.en: a single episode filmed to see whether a series will work
branches.cn: 先拍一集，看整部剧能否成立

intro.en: The word is carried by a disputed Greek oar, a medieval Latin helmsman, its Italian and French forms, and two English suffixes that name the trade and its absence.
intro.cn: 这个词由有争议的希腊语「桨」、中世纪拉丁语的掌舵者、它的意大利语与法语形式，以及两个表示行业与「无人」的英语后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Only the medieval Latin form is safely attested; the older Greek oar is offered as a possibility rather than a settled fact.
latinIntro.cn: 只有中世纪拉丁语形式有可靠记载；更早的希腊语「桨」只是作为一种可能提出，并非定论。

items.meaning: the work of guiding ships, and the fee for it

definition_zh: 别针；大头针；饰针；插脚；钉住；按住
definition_en: a short thin piece of metal with a sharp point used to fasten things, a decorative brooch, a metal leg on a plug, and the act of holding something firmly in place
core_image: 一枚银亮的别针穿过布料，针尖从另一面探出来
scene: 裁缝铺的午后，长桌上铺满布料，粉笔画的线还很清楚。She fixed the paper pattern to the cloth with a pin before cutting.
sceneCN: 这里的 pin 是「别针、大头针」（第 1 个义项：固定布料的细针）；句意是她用一枚别针把纸样固定在布上，然后才下剪。图中可辨识物件：布料、粉笔线、剪刀。

derivatives.zh: 由 pin 与 hole 复合而成，义为「针孔」
由 pin 与 point 复合而成，义为「精确定位」
由 pin 与 head 复合而成，义为「针头；傻瓜」
由 pin 与 prick 复合而成，义为「针刺般的小孔；刺痛」

senses.title: A short pointed fastener
senses.definition: a short thin piece of metal with a sharp point and a head, used to fasten cloth or paper
senses.definitionCN: 一端尖锐、一端有头的小金属件，用来固定布料或纸张
senses.example: A pin held the two sheets of paper together.
senses.exampleCN: 一枚别针把两张纸固定在一起。
senses.why: Old English pinn named a peg or bolt, and the small pointed fastener kept both the shape and the name.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 pinn 指木钉或销子，这种带尖的小固定件既保留了它的形状，也继承了它的名字。

senses.title: A decorative brooch
senses.definition: a small ornamental pin worn on clothing for decoration
senses.definitionCN: 别在衣物上作装饰的小饰针
senses.example: She fastened a gold pin to her collar.
senses.exampleCN: 她把一枚金饰针别在衣领上。
senses.why: Once a pin could hold cloth, it could also hold an ornament, and the jewel fixed on the pin took over the word.
senses.whyCN: 既然别针能固定布料，也就能固定饰物，于是别在针上的珠宝接管了这个词。

senses.title: To fasten or hold firmly
senses.definition: to fasten something with a pin, or to press and hold it so that it cannot move
senses.definitionCN: 用别针固定某物，或压住使其不能移动
senses.example: Pin the hem before you sew it.
senses.exampleCN: 缝之前先把折边别住。
senses.why: The tool became an action in the usual English way: to pin is simply to do what a pin does, hold two things together.
senses.whyCN: 这个工具按英语的惯常方式变成了动作：to pin 就是做别针做的事，把两样东西固定在一起。

senses.title: A metal leg on a plug or chip
senses.definition: one of the metal legs on an electrical plug or component that makes contact with a socket
senses.definitionCN: 插头或电子元件上用来与插座接触的金属脚
senses.example: One pin on the plug was bent, so it would not fit.
senses.exampleCN: 插头上的一个插脚弯了，所以插不进去。
senses.why: Electronics needed a name for the small metal legs pushed into a socket, and their shape and job matched the old fastener exactly.
senses.whyCN: 电子行业需要给插进插座的细小金属脚命名，而它们的形状和用处与旧日的别针完全吻合。

intro.en: Pin is an Old English word for a peg, and the peg itself is usually traced to a Latin word for a point or feather.
intro.cn: pin 是古英语中表示钉子的词，而这种钉子一般认为源自拉丁语中表示「尖端、羽毛」的词。

items.en: Pinna meant a feather, a wing or a point, and it also named the pointed crest of a wall.
items.cn: pinna 指羽毛、翅膀或尖端，也指墙头突出的尖顶。

items.en: Germanic speakers borrowed the Latin point word and used it for a peg; the reconstructed form is usually written with an asterisk, as the borrowing route is not certain.
items.cn: 日耳曼诸语借用了拉丁语中表示「尖端」的词来指木钉；重构形式通常带星号，因为借入路径并不确定。

items.en: Old English pinn covered a peg, a bolt and a small pointed fastener.
items.cn: 古英语 pinn 兼指木钉、销子和小型尖头固定件。

items.en: Middle English pin narrowed towards the small pointed fastener used on cloth.
items.cn: 中古英语 pin 收窄到用来固定布料的小尖针。

items.en: Modern English extended the word to jewellery, to the legs of electrical plugs, and to phrases such as pin down.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义扩展到首饰、插头插脚，以及 pin down 一类的说法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that merely share letters with pin; the near-meaning group collects other small things that hold material together.
note.cn: 形近组收只是与 pin 拼写相近的词；近义组收其他把材料固定在一起的小物件。

entries.definition: An evergreen tree, or to long for something.
entries.definitionCN: 常绿树；也指渴望。

entries.definition: To turn round quickly, or to draw out thread.
entries.definitionCN: 快速旋转；也指纺线。

entries.definition: A tool for writing with ink.
entries.definitionCN: 用墨水写字的工具。

entries.definition: A short nail with a wide flat head.
entries.definitionCN: 短而钉帽宽平的钉子。

entries.definition: A thin pointed tool used for sewing.
entries.definitionCN: 缝纫用的细尖工具。

entries.definition: A small object that holds papers together.
entries.definitionCN: 夹住纸张的小物件。

normalIntro.en: The word is a point that holds things, and every sense keeps something small, sharp or metal at its centre.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个能固定东西的尖端，每个义项的核心都离不了小而尖或小而硬的金属。

normal.en: Pin comes from a Latin word for a point, and every sense still turns on something small and sharp.
normal.cn: pin 来自拉丁语中表示「尖端」的词，每个义项都围绕某个小而尖的东西。

normal.en: Pinhole, pinpoint and pinprick are all built on the same tiny measure, the size of a pin.
normal.cn: pinhole、pinpoint 与 pinprick 都建立在同一个微小的尺度上：一枚别针的大小。

normal.en: Pinhead first meant the head of a pin, and only later became an insult about a small brain.
normal.cn: pinhead 最早指别针的针头，后来才变成说人脑子小的贬称。

normal.en: To pin down is to fix something the way a pin fixes cloth, so a physical act becomes an abstract one.
normal.cn: to pin down 是像别针固定布料那样把事情定住，身体动作由此变成抽象动作。

normal.en: Safety pin and drawing pin put the purpose first, the usual English pattern for compounds.
normal.cn: safety pin 与 drawing pin 把用途放在前面，这是英语复合词的常见模式。

abstract.en: A pin holds things together by being almost nothing, a single point of contact.
abstract.cn: 别针几乎什么都不是，只靠一个接触点就把东西固定住。

abstract.en: Pin down, pin on, pin hopes on: the small metal object becomes a way of fixing blame, facts and hope.
abstract.cn: pin down、pin on、pin hopes on：这枚小金属件变成了固定责任、事实和希望的动词。

abstract.en: What is pinned can also be unpinned, which is why the word carries a hint of something temporary.
abstract.cn: 别住的东西也可以取下来，所以这个词总带着一点临时的意味。

examples.en: A pin held the two sheets of paper together.
examples.cn: 一枚别针把两张纸固定在一起。

examples.en: Pin the hem before you sew it.
examples.cn: 缝之前先把折边别住。

examples.en: One pin on the plug was bent, so it would not fit.
examples.cn: 插头上的一个插脚弯了，所以插不进去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拼」——用别针把两块布拼在一起，这个动作就叫 pin。

root: 古英语 pinn（钉、销）一般认为借自拉丁语 pinna（羽毛、尖端），由「尖」的意象引申为细小的金属别针。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a small pointed metal object; the senses branch into ornament, into the act of fixing, and into the metal legs of modern plugs.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是带尖的小金属件；义项分向装饰、固定的动作，以及现代插头上的金属脚。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bright pin passing through cloth, its point showing on the other side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚银亮的别针穿过布料，针尖从另一面透出来。

branches.en: two sheets of paper held together by one thin point
branches.cn: 两张纸被一个细尖固定在一起

branches.en: a small gold ornament on a coat collar
branches.cn: 大衣领子上的一枚小金饰

branches.en: a hem held flat under the machine needle
branches.cn: 折边被压平送进缝纫机针下

branches.en: the same small object doing its same small job
branches.cn: 同一个小物件重复着同一件小事

branches.en: a bent metal leg that will not enter the socket
branches.cn: 弯曲的金属插脚插不进插座

intro.en: The word is built on a Latin point, an Old English peg, and four English compounds that all measure something by the size of a pin.
intro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语的「尖端」、古英语的「木钉」，以及四个以别针大小来衡量的英语复合词之上。

latinIntro.en: Latin pinna supplies the point at the root of the word, and the reconstructed Germanic peg is the form that carried it into English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pinna 提供了这个词根部的「尖端」，重构的日耳曼语「木钉」则是把它带进英语的形式。

the head of a pin; a foolish person
a tiny hole or a sharp little pain

definition_zh: 松树；松木；渴望；憔悴
definition_en: a tall evergreen tree with needle-shaped leaves, its pale soft wood, or to long for someone so much that you grow thin and dull
core_image: 雪坡上一棵针叶树，细长的针叶托着雪，树皮裂成一片片鳞甲
scene: 冬天的山坡上，一排针叶树顶着雪，树皮裂成一片片鳞甲，风穿过细针一样的叶子发出低低的响声。The old pine at the gate has stood there for a hundred years.
sceneCN: 这里 pine 指「松树」（第 1 个义项：常绿的针叶乔木）；句意为门口那棵老松已经在那里站了一百年。图中可辨识物件：雪坡、针叶、开裂的树皮。

derivatives.zh: 由 pine 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「松树的；松林多的」
由 pine 加表场所的后缀 -ery 构成，义为「松林；松园」
由 pine 加 -ing 构成，义为「苦苦思念；日渐消瘦」

senses.title: An evergreen tree with needle-shaped leaves
senses.definition: a tall evergreen tree with needle-shaped leaves and woody cones that stays green through the winter
senses.definitionCN: 一种高大的常绿乔木，叶如细针，结木质球果，冬季依然青绿
senses.example: An old pine shades the whole yard.
senses.exampleCN: 一棵老松为整个院子遮阴。
senses.why: Latin pinus was simply the name of this tree, and English borrowed the noun together with the tree, so this is the sense the word started from.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pinus 本来就是这种树的名字，英语连同树一起借来这个名词，所以这是词最原始的义项。

senses.title: The pale soft wood of this tree
senses.definition: the light, soft timber of this tree, used for floors, furniture and paper
senses.definitionCN: 这种树浅色而柔软的木材，用于地板、家具与造纸
senses.example: The floor is made of pine.
senses.exampleCN: 地板是松木做的。
senses.why: Once a tree has a name, its timber takes the same name, because the material is only the tree after it has been cut and sawn.
senses.whyCN: 一种树有了名字，它的木材也就用同一个名字，因为木料不过是砍下锯开之后的树。

senses.title: To long for someone or something
senses.definition: to want someone or something very much, in a way that makes you unhappy
senses.definitionCN: 非常想要某人或某物，想到心里难受
senses.example: She pined for the sea she had left behind.
senses.exampleCN: 她苦苦思念着离开的那片海。
senses.why: The verb came from a different word, an Old English verb for torment; a longing that hurts was pictured as a slow torture, and that ache stayed inside the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 动词另有来源，是古英语中表示「折磨」的动词；令人难受的渴望被想象成一种缓慢的拷问，这份痛感就留在了词义里。

senses.title: To waste away with grief or longing
senses.definition: to become weak, thin and dull because of sorrow, illness or a long wait
senses.definitionCN: 因悲伤、疾病或长久等待而变得虚弱、消瘦、没有神采
senses.example: He pined away after the farm was sold.
senses.exampleCN: 农场卖掉之后，他日渐憔悴。
senses.why: If longing is a torture, the body eventually shows it; pine away names the visible result of that inner strain rather than the feeling itself.
senses.whyCN: 既然渴望是一种折磨，身体迟早会把它显出来；pine away 指的就是这份内在煎熬露在外表上的结果，而不是那股情绪本身。

intro.en: Two different words meet in this spelling: the tree name came from Latin pinus, while the verb for painful longing came from an Old English verb for tormenting.
intro.cn: 这个拼写里其实合流了两个不同的词：树名来自拉丁语 pinus，表示痛苦渴望的动词则来自古英语中表示折磨的动词。

items.en: Latin pinus named the pine tree and could also mean its wood or resin; the same name travelled around the Mediterranean.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pinus 是松树的名字，也可指松木或松脂；同一个名称在地中海各地通行。

items.en: Old English borrowed the tree name as pin, and the modern spelling later added a final e to match the verb.
items.cn: 古英语把树名借入写作 pin，现代拼写后来加了一个词尾 e，好与动词的写法统一。

items.en: A separate Old English verb pinian meant to torture or torment; it came from pin, a noun for pain that is generally traced back to Latin poena.
items.cn: 另有一个古英语动词 pinian，意为折磨、拷问；它来自表示痛苦的名词 pin，而这个词一般认为可追溯到拉丁语 poena。

items.en: Middle English kept both words, so pinen could mean to suffer and also to yearn painfully for something lost.
items.cn: 中古英语把两个词都保留下来，于是 pinen 既指受苦，也指为失去的东西痛苦地思念。

items.en: Modern English holds the tree, its timber, the ache of longing and the visible wasting away, with the two histories now written as one word.
items.cn: 现代英语同时容纳了树、木材、思念之苦与看得见的消瘦，两段来历如今写成同一个词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the tree's own family and a few words that only look similar; the near-meaning group pairs other conifers with other verbs of longing.
note.cn: 形近组收这棵树自己的词族，以及几个只是看起来相似的词；近义组把其他针叶树与别的「渴望」动词配在一起。

entries.definition: A small thin piece of metal for fastening cloth; it comes from a Latin word for a point or peg, so it is close in spelling but not in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 固定布料用的小金属针；它来自拉丁语中表示尖点或木钉的词，所以只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Shaped like a pine cone, as in the small gland deep in the brain.
entries.definitionCN: 形状像松果的，如大脑深处那个小腺体。

entries.definition: The fruit was named after the pine cone, which early English speakers thought it resembled.
entries.definitionCN: 这种水果因外形被早期英语使用者比作松果而得名。

entries.definition: A place where pine trees are grown.
entries.definitionCN: 种植松树的地方；松林。

entries.definition: A tall evergreen tree with flat needles and upright cones.
entries.definitionCN: 一种高大的常绿树，叶扁平，球果直立；冷杉。

entries.definition: An evergreen tree with short needles and hanging cones.
entries.definitionCN: 一种常绿树，针叶短，球果下垂；云杉。

entries.definition: A tree with needle-like leaves that turn yellow and fall in autumn.
entries.definitionCN: 针叶在秋天变黄脱落的树；落叶松。

entries.definition: To feel a strong, sad desire for something.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物怀有强烈而带苦味的向往。

normalIntro.en: A tree name and a verb of torment happen to share one spelling, and the whole family divides neatly between wood and longing.
normalIntro.cn: 一个树名和一个表示折磨的动词恰好共用一个拼写，整个词族也就清楚地分成「木」与「渴望」两半。

normal.en: Latin pinus is the tree, which is why botany still uses pinus for the genus and why pine needles resist frost.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pinus 就是这种树，所以植物学至今用 pinus 作属名，松针也才那么耐霜。

normal.en: The verb pine never grew out of the tree; it came from an Old English word for torment, so pine for and pine tree are only spelling twins.
normal.cn: 动词 pine 并不是从树长出来的，它来自古英语中表示折磨的词，所以 pine for 与 pine tree 只是拼写上的双胞胎。

normal.en: Pine away adds away to the verb: the person is not only longing but visibly losing weight and colour.
normal.cn: pine away 在动词后加 away：人不只是思念，还肉眼可见地掉肉、褪色。

normal.en: Pinery uses -ery, the same place suffix as in bakery and brewery, so it means a place of pines.
normal.cn: pinery 用 -ery，与 bakery、brewery 里那个表场所的后缀相同，所以意思是「松树之地」。

normal.en: Pineal keeps the cone image: the gland was named for its shape, not for any connection with timber.
normal.cn: pineal 保留了松果的形象：那个腺体是因形状得名，与木材没有关系。

abstract.en: A pine keeps its needles all winter, and English keeps two unrelated words under one spelling just as stubbornly.
abstract.cn: 松树整个冬天都不落叶，英语也同样固执地把两个不相干的词留在一个拼写下。

abstract.en: The same four letters can mean shade, floorboards, heartache and weight loss, which is a reminder that context does the sorting.
abstract.cn: 同样四个字母可以指树荫、地板、心痛与消瘦，这提醒人：分辨词义的是上下文。

abstract.en: To pine is to be pulled toward something absent; the tree simply stands where it is, which is why the two images never mix.
abstract.cn: pine 是被拉向缺席之物；而松树只是站在原地，所以这两个意象从不混淆。

examples.en: An old pine shades the whole yard.
examples.cn: 一棵老松为整个院子遮阴。

examples.en: She pined for the sea she had left behind.
examples.cn: 她苦苦思念着离开的那片海。

examples.en: The floor is made of pine.
examples.cn: 地板是松木做的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拍嗯」——拍着树干嗯一声，抬头就是松树；记住 pine 是松，也指为思念而瘦。

root: 树义来自拉丁语 pinus（松树）；动词义来自古英语 pinian（折磨），其名词 pin（痛苦）一般认为源自拉丁语 poena。两个来源不同，现代拼写合流。

sensesIntro.en: The tree sense stands at the centre; the timber follows the tree, and a separate verb of torment gives the two senses of painful longing and visible wasting.
sensesIntro.cn: 树义处在中心；木材义跟着树走，而另一个表示折磨的动词带来「痛苦思念」与「肉眼可见的消瘦」两个义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a snow-loaded conifer standing still while someone far away is missed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一棵压着雪的针叶树静静立着，而远处有人正被苦苦思念。

branches.en: needles holding snow without breaking
branches.cn: 针叶托住积雪却不断

branches.en: pale boards stacked beside a saw
branches.cn: 锯旁堆着的浅色木板

branches.en: a letter written and never sent
branches.cn: 一封写好却没寄出的信

branches.en: a chair by the window growing thinner by the month
branches.cn: 窗边的椅子一月比一月空瘦

branches.en: a wait long enough to show on the face
branches.cn: 久到写在脸上的等待

intro.en: The word is supported by a Latin tree name, an Old English noun and verb for pain, and the endings that turn it into a place and a shape.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语树名、古英语中表示痛苦的名词与动词，以及把它变成场所与形状的词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: The tree comes from one Latin word and the ache of longing from another; both links are well attested, unlike the folk guess that the verb grew out of the tree.
latinIntro.cn: 树义与思念之苦分别来自两个不同的拉丁词；这两条联系都有充分证据，反倒是「动词由树长出来」的说法只是民间猜测。

definition_zh: 音高；音调；球场；投掷；搭（帐篷）；沥青；推销话术
definition_en: the highness or lowness of a sound, a marked sports ground, a forceful throw, the setting up of a tent, or the black substance tar
core_image: 投手在土丘上抬起前腿，把球沿一条压低了的直线送向本垒
scene: 傍晚的板球场上，草地被修剪得整整齐齐，两队球员正走向场中央。The players walked slowly across the pitch before the match began.
sceneCN: 这里是「球场」（第 2 个义项：板球、足球等比赛用的划定场地）；句意为比赛开始前球员们慢慢走过球场。画面里是被修剪整齐的草皮和走向场中央的球员。

pos.zh: 音高；音调；球场；沥青；推销话术

derivatives.zh: 由 pitch 加表示施动者的 -er 构成，指棒球中的投手，也指带嘴的大水壶
由 pitch（沥青）加 -y 构成，形容沥青般的、漆黑的
由 pitch 与 fork 复合而成，指翻挑干草用的长柄叉

senses.title: The highness or lowness of a sound
senses.definition: the degree to which a sound is high or low
senses.definitionCN: 声音听起来高或低的程度
senses.example: Her voice dropped to a lower pitch as she reached the last line.
senses.exampleCN: 念到最后一行时，她的声音降到了更低的音高。
senses.why: The musical sense is generally connected with placing a note at a fixed level rather than with throwing, though the exact middle step in the record is uncertain.
senses.whyCN: 音乐上的这一义项一般认为和「把一个音安放在确定的高度」有关，而不是从投掷来的；不过文献里中间那一步的具体来历仍有不确定之处。

senses.title: A marked ground for a sport
senses.definition: an area of ground marked out for a sport such as football or cricket
senses.definitionCN: 为足球、板球等运动划出的场地
senses.example: The ball rolled off the pitch and into the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 球滚出球场，飞进了人群。
senses.why: A cricket pitch was first the prepared strip between the wickets, levelled and marked by setting stakes, so the ground took its name from the act of fixing it.
senses.whyCN: 板球的 pitch 最初指三柱门之间那条经过整平、用木桩标定的长条地面；场地因为被「固定、标定」过而得名，「设置」的动作就这样变成了「场地」这个名词。

senses.title: To throw with force and aim
senses.definition: to throw something with a planned aim, especially in baseball or cricket
senses.definitionCN: 有目标地用力投出，尤指棒球或板球中的投球
senses.example: He pitched the ball so low that the batter stepped back.
senses.exampleCN: 他把球投得那么低，击球手都往后缩了一步。
senses.why: The old verb meant to set or thrust something firmly, and throwing was felt as driving an object away along a chosen line, a sense that now lives mainly in ball games.
senses.whyCN: 古时的动词本指把东西牢牢安放或猛力一送；投掷被理解成把物体沿选定的线路送出去，这层意思如今主要活在球类运动里，「投」因此是从「送、安置」长出来的。

senses.title: To set up a tent or a camp
senses.definition: to put up a tent or arrange a camp for a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 支起帐篷，或临时布置营地
senses.example: We pitched the tent on the driest patch of grass we could find.
senses.exampleCN: 我们把帐篷搭在能找到的最干的一块草地上。
senses.why: This is the most concrete sense of fixing something upright: the verb names driving the poles so that the shelter stands, and camping kept the literal image alive.
senses.whyCN: 这是「把东西立起来固定住」最具体的用法：动词指把支杆钉稳、让遮蔽物立住，露营一直保留着这个字面画面，所以「搭帐篷」就是「把帐篷固定在地上」。

senses.title: A thick black substance made from tar
senses.definition: a thick black sticky substance made from tar, used on roofs and roads
senses.definitionCN: 由焦油制成的浓稠黑色黏性物质，用来铺路或涂屋顶
senses.example: The roof was sealed with hot pitch.
senses.exampleCN: 屋顶用滚烫的沥青封住了。
senses.why: This sense belongs to a different word that fell into the same spelling: Old English pic came from Latin pix, and the black tar has nothing to do with throwing or with sound.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项其实来自另一个词，只是碰巧拼成了同一个样子：古英语 pic 出自拉丁语 pix（沥青）；这层「黑而黏」的意思与投掷、声音毫无渊源，属于同形异源。

intro.en: Two histories meet in one spelling: a Latin word for tar and an English verb of setting and throwing whose deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: 两种来历在同一个拼写里相遇：一个是表示沥青的拉丁词，一个是表示安放与投掷的英语动词，后者更早的来源并不确定。

items.en: Pix, with the genitive picis, meant pitch or tar, and it is the source of the Old English word for the black substance.
items.cn: pix 的属格是 picis，意为沥青、焦油，是古英语中表示这种黑色物质的词的来源。

items.en: Old English pic named the tar-like material and survives in compounds such as pitch-black and pitchfork.
items.cn: 古英语 pic 指这种类似焦油的物质，并保留在 pitch-black、pitchfork 这类复合词里。

items.en: A verb picchen is recorded for setting, fixing or thrusting something; its deeper origin is uncertain and may have nothing to do with the tar word.
items.cn: 中古英语有一个动词 picchen，表示安放、固定或猛推某物；它更早的来源不确定，可能和表示沥青的那个词毫无关系。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the verb covered pitching a tent, marking out a wicket and throwing a ball, and the noun named the prepared ground.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个动词已兼指搭帐篷、标出板球三柱门以及投球，名词则用来指那块整理好的场地。

items.en: Modern English adds musical pitch and the sales pitch, while the tar sense remains in roofing and road work.
items.cn: 现代英语又添上「音高」与「推销话术」，而沥青义仍留在屋顶与道路工程里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the verb and spellings that merely resemble it; the near-meaning group gathers words for sound level, sports ground, throwing and tar.
note.cn: 形近组收由这个动词构成的形式以及仅仅外形相似的拼写；近义组收表示音高、球场、投掷与沥青的词。

entries.definition: The past tense of the verb, and also an adjective describing a roof's slope or a tone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词的过去式，也用来形容屋顶的坡度或某种音调。

entries.definition: A baseball player who throws the ball, or a jug with a lip for pouring.
entries.definitionCN: 棒球中投球的人，或倒液体用的带嘴壶。

entries.definition: A painting, drawing or photograph; the spelling is close but the root is different.
entries.definitionCN: 绘画、素描或照片；拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A long-handled fork used for lifting and turning hay.
entries.definitionCN: 翻挑干草用的长柄叉。

entries.definition: The quality or height of a sound.
entries.definitionCN: 声音的音质或高低。

entries.definition: An area of ground used for sport.
entries.definitionCN: 用于运动的场地。

entries.definition: To send something through the air with the hand.
entries.definitionCN: 用手把东西抛向空中。

entries.definition: A thick black sticky substance used on roads and roofs.
entries.definitionCN: 铺路与涂屋顶用的浓稠黑色黏性物质。

normalIntro.en: A Latin word for tar, an English verb of setting and throwing, and the grounds and sounds that verb prepared all share one spelling.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示沥青的拉丁词、一个表示安放与投掷的英语动词，以及这个动词所准备的场地与声音，共用同一个拼写。

normal.en: Latin pix gave Old English pic, so the tar sense is the oldest and most securely traced part of the word.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pix 送来古英语 pic，所以沥青义是这个词里最古老、来历也最清楚的一支。

normal.en: The verb picchen meant to fix or thrust, which is why we pitch a tent, pitch a wicket and pitch a ball.
normal.cn: 动词 picchen 意为固定或猛推，所以我们搭帐篷、标出三柱门、投球都用 pitch。

normal.en: A cricket pitch is not the whole field but the prepared strip between the wickets, named after the fixing of the stumps.
normal.cn: 板球的 pitch 并不是整片场地，而是三柱门之间那条整理过的长条地面，名字来自把门柱固定下来的动作。

normal.en: Musical pitch is usually explained by placing a note at a fixed level, although the exact link is not certain.
normal.cn: 音乐上的音高通常用「把一个音安放在确定高度」来解释，不过确切的中间环节并不确定。

normal.en: The past tense is pitched, with -ed added to a word that already ends in a ch sound.
normal.cn: 过去式是 pitched，在本来就以 ch 音收尾的词后加 -ed。

abstract.en: One spelling holds two unrelated lives: black tar from Latin and the act of setting or throwing from an uncertain English verb.
abstract.cn: 一个拼写装着两种互不相干的来历：来自拉丁语的黑色沥青，以及来自来历不明的英语动词的「安放、投掷」。

abstract.en: Pitch always implies a chosen line, whether it is a ball to a batter, a note to a scale or a tent pole to the ground.
abstract.cn: pitch 总带着一条选定的线：球飞向击球手，音落在音阶上，帐篷杆扎进地里。

abstract.en: A sales pitch borrows the thrower's aim: words are sent at a listener along a line chosen in advance.
abstract.cn: 推销话术借用了投手的瞄准：话沿着事先选好的线路，被送向听者。

examples.en: The players walked across the pitch before the match began.
examples.cn: 比赛开始前，球员们走过球场。

examples.en: She pitched the ball straight over the plate.
examples.cn: 她把球直直地投过了本垒板。

examples.en: The old roof was covered with pitch.
examples.cn: 旧屋顶上铺着一层沥青。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「劈球」——投手把球一劈手就丢向本垒；pitch 就是投掷，也指音高与球场。

root: 「沥青」义来自拉丁语 pix（沥青）；表示投、固定、搭起的动词一支一般认为出自中古英语 picchen（安放、猛推），更早来源不确定；音高与球场都由「固定在某一位置」引申。

sensesIntro.en: The core image is a chosen line along which something is sent or fixed; it branches into the ball, the marked ground, the standing tent, the fixed note and the unrelated black tar.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心意象是一条选定的线，东西沿着它被送出或被固定；由此分出投出的球、标出的场地、立起的帐篷、定住的音高，以及另一支毫无关系的黑色沥青。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pitcher on the mound lifting his front leg and sending the ball down a chosen line to the plate.
core.cn: 核心意象：投手在土丘上抬起前腿，把球沿一条选定的线路送往本垒。

branches.cn: 球从低处飞过本垒板

branches.en: white lines marking a strip of grass
branches.cn: 白线划出的一条草地

branches.en: a tent rising pole by pole
branches.cn: 帐篷一根杆一根杆立起

branches.en: a string tightened until the note holds
branches.cn: 琴弦绷紧，音高稳住

branches.cn: 滚烫的沥青浇上屋顶

intro.en: A Latin noun for tar, the Old English noun it produced, an English verb of setting and throwing, and three English suffixes and compounds hold the word together.
intro.cn: 表示沥青的拉丁名词、由它而来的古英语名词、表示安放与投掷的英语动词，以及三个英语后缀与复合词，共同撑起这个词。

latinIntro.en: Only the tar sense has clear Latin ancestry in pix; the verb of setting and throwing is of uncertain origin and is not derived from that noun.
latinIntro.cn: 只有沥青义在 pix 里有清楚的拉丁来历；表示安放与投掷的动词来源不确定，并非由那个名词派生。

definition_en: a large area of flat land; simple and without decoration; easy to understand; direct and honest

senses.title: A large area of flat land
senses.definition: a broad area of land with little or no change in height
senses.definitionCN: 高度起伏很小或没有起伏的大片陆地
senses.example: A dry plain stretches beyond the last row of trees.
senses.exampleCN: 过了最后一排树，一片干燥的平原一直延伸出去。
senses.why: Latin planus meant 'flat, level'; the noun names ground that offers no rise to stop the eye.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 planus 意为「平的、水平的」；这个名词指不提供任何隆起阻挡视线的地方。

senses.title: Flat country in the plural
senses.definition: the plains, used for a whole region of flat open country
senses.definitionCN: 用复数指一整片平坦开阔的地区
senses.example: Storms move quickly across the plains.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴快速掠过这片平原地区。
senses.why: The plural turns a stretch of flat ground into a named region, as with the mountains.
senses.whyCN: 复数把一段平地变成一个有名字的地区，就像「山脉」一词的用法一样。

senses.title: Simple and undecorated
senses.definition: without ornament, pattern or unnecessary detail
senses.definitionCN: 没有装饰、花纹或不必要的细节
senses.example: She wore a plain grey dress to the ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿了一件素灰色连衣裙去参加典礼。
senses.why: A surface with nothing added is metaphorically level: no raised ornament, no pattern.
senses.whyCN: 没有附加任何东西的表面在比喻上是「平的」：没有凸起的装饰，也没有花纹。

senses.title: Easy to understand
senses.definition: expressed so clearly that no explanation is needed
senses.definitionCN: 表达得足够清楚，无需再解释
senses.example: The instructions were written in plain English.
senses.exampleCN: 这些说明用平实的英语写成。
senses.why: Clear speech is flat ground: nothing in the way, no obstacle between meaning and listener.
senses.whyCN: 清楚的话就是平地：中间没有障碍，意思与听者之间没有阻隔。

senses.title: Direct and honest in speech
senses.definition: saying what is true without softening or hiding it
senses.definitionCN: 不加缓和、不加遮掩地说出真实情况
senses.example: He gave a plain answer that surprised everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 他给了一个直率的回答，让所有人都吃了一惊。
senses.why: Plainness removes cover: what is said is exactly what is meant, with no decorative evasion.
senses.whyCN: 朴素意味着去掉遮盖：说出来的就是本意，没有任何装饰性的回避。

senses.title: Ordinary in appearance
senses.definition: not beautiful or striking in face or style
senses.definitionCN: 面容或风格不出众、不引人注目
senses.example: He was a plain man with a quiet voice.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个相貌平常、声音安静的人。
senses.why: The same 'nothing added' idea applies to looks: no feature stands out.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「没有附加」的想法也用于外貌：没有哪个特征特别突出。

senses.title: Basic and unelaborate
senses.definition: simple in composition, as food or clothing with nothing extra
senses.definitionCN: 构成简单，如不加额外调料的食物或衣物
senses.example: They ate plain bread and cheese by the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在火边吃简单的面包和奶酪。
senses.why: Plain food has nothing added to it, so the adjective marks the absence of extras.
senses.whyCN: 这类食物就是没有额外添加的东西，因此这个形容词标记的是「没有附加」。

senses.title: Complete and obvious
senses.definition: used for emphasis to mean sheer or unmistakable
senses.definitionCN: 用于强调，表示纯粹的、显而易见的
senses.example: That is plain nonsense from beginning to end.
senses.exampleCN: 那从头到尾都是十足的胡扯。
senses.why: What is obvious needs no ornament or argument; the flat sense becomes an intensifier.
senses.whyCN: 显而易见的东西不需要装饰或论证；平坦义于是变成强调词。

intro.en: Plain the noun and plain the adjective come from the same Latin adjective planus 'flat'; the two uses merged in English. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 名词 plain 与形容词 plain 都来自同一个拉丁形容词 planus「平的」；两种用法在英语中合并。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin planus meant 'flat, level, even' and, figuratively, 'clear, plain'; the neuter noun planum meant 'a flat surface'.
items.cn: 拉丁 planus 意为「平的、平的、均匀的」，引申为「清楚的、明白的」；中性名词 planum 指「平面」。

items.en: Planities 'level ground, plain' supplied the landscape noun; it is built on the same stem as planus.
items.cn: planities「平地、平原」提供了地貌名词，它与 planus 同词干。

items.en: Old French plain carried both the adjective 'flat, simple' and the noun 'flat country' into English.
items.cn: 古法语 plain 同时把形容词「平的、朴素的」与名词「平地」带进了英语。

items.en: Middle English kept both, and the adjective developed the senses 'clear', 'honest', 'ordinary' and 'simple' from the idea of having nothing added.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了两者；形容词从「没有附加」这一想法发展出「清楚」「直率」「平常」「简单」等义。

items.en: Fixed compounds such as flood plain, plain clothes and plain English settled in the modern period and mark the separate senses.
items.cn: flood plain、plain clothes、plain English 等固定复合词在近代固定下来，标出各自不同的义项。

items.en: The Latin layer is secure; only the first dates are approximate. Any deeper Indo-European source for planus is a reconstruction and is not asserted here.
items.cn: 拉丁层次可靠，只有首见年代为约数。planus 更深的印欧来源属重构，此处不作断言。

note.en: The first group holds words built on or resembling plan-; the second holds words for flat open country.
note.cn: 第一组是与 plan- 同源或形近的词；第二组是表示平坦开阔地区的词。

entries.definition: A flat surface, a tool or an aircraft; it comes from Latin planum and is related, but it never means open country or simple style.
entries.definitionCN: 平面、刨子或飞机；来自拉丁 planum，与 plain 相关，但从不表示开阔乡野或朴素风格。

entries.definition: A intended arrangement of future actions; the vowel is short /æ/, not long /eɪ/.
entries.definitionCN: 对未来行动的安排；元音是短音 /æ/，不是长音 /eɪ/。

entries.definition: To make something clear; Latin explanare is built on planus 'flat', so it shares the root but is not a derivative of the English plain.
entries.definitionCN: 把某事讲清楚；拉丁 explanare 建立在 planus「平的」上，因此同根，但不是英语 plain 的派生词。

entries.definition: A formal complaint or lament; it ends in -t and belongs to a different legal and literary family.
entries.definitionCN: 正式的申诉或哀诉；以 -t 结尾，属另一个法律与文学词族。

entries.definition: A large flat grassland, especially in North America; it stresses grass cover, while plain stresses flatness.
entries.definitionCN: 大片平坦草原，尤指北美；强调草被，而 plain 强调平坦。

entries.definition: A vast dry grass plain in Eurasia; it is a regional and ecological term, not a general one.
entries.definitionCN: 欧亚大陆广阔干旱的草原平原；它是区域性与生态学术语，不是一般词。

entries.definition: Land that is flat, used mainly in geography; it says only what plain already says.
entries.definitionCN: 平坦的陆地，主要用于地理学；它只是把 plain 已有的意思说出来。

entries.definition: A tropical grassland with scattered trees; it is defined by climate and vegetation, not by flatness.
entries.definitionCN: 散布树木的热带草原；它按气候与植被定义，而非平坦程度。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin planus root, the real compounds and the split between land and style.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁 planus 词根、真实的复合词，以及「土地」与「风格」两条义线。

normal.en: Latin planus 'flat' gives both the land and the style: flat ground, nothing added.
normal.cn: 拉丁 planus「平的」同时给出土地与风格：平地，以及没有附加。

normal.en: The family runs plain, plains, plainly, plainness, plainspoken.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 plain、plains、plainly、plainness、plainspoken。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: wide plain, plain English, plain clothes, flood plain.
normal.cn: 固定搭配有 wide plain、plain English、plain clothes、flood plain。

normal.en: Explain shares the root planus 'flat': to explain is literally to make level.
normal.cn: explain 共享 planus「平的」词根：explain 字面上就是「使平」。

normal.en: Plain is flat; prairie is grassy; steppe is dry. Each picks a different feature.
normal.cn: plain 强调平，prairie 强调草，steppe 强调干旱；各取一个特征。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet of paper laid on the ground, stretching to every horizon.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸铺在地上，一直伸到每一条地平线。

abstract.en: Picture a room with no pictures, no pattern and no colour but grey.
abstract.cn: 想象一个房间没有画、没有花纹，除了灰色没有别的颜色。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence with no metaphor, no decoration and no hidden meaning.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话没有比喻、没有装饰，也没有隐藏的意思。

examples.en: The plain is used for wheat and cattle.
examples.cn: 这片平原用来种小麦和养牛。

examples.en: Please say it in plain language so everyone can follow.
examples.cn: 请用平实的语言说，让每个人都能听懂。

examples.en: The plain truth is that the plan will cost too much.
examples.cn: 明摆着的事实是，这个计划花费太高。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普（pu）+ 兰（lan）」—— 普通又平坦、一眼看到边的大地 → 平原；朴素的

root: 拉丁 planus「平的、清楚的」→ 古法语 plain（形容词与名词）→ 英语 plain；名词义与形容词义同源合并。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses split into two lines from one root: flat land on one side, and 'nothing added' on the other, giving simple, clear, honest, ordinary and basic.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个词根分成两条线：一边是平坦的土地，另一边是「没有附加」，由此得到朴素、清楚、直率、平常与简单。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a surface with no rise and no added ornament, so nothing blocks the view.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个既没有隆起也没有附加装饰的表面，因此什么都挡不住视线。

branches.en: THE LAND: a flat stretch, and the plural that makes it a region.
branches.cn: 土地：一段平地，以及把它变成地区的复数。

branches.en: NOTHING ADDED: undecorated clothes, ordinary looks and plain food.
branches.cn: 没有附加：无装饰的衣服、平常的相貌与简单的食物。

branches.en: NO OBSTACLE: clear language is flat ground between speaker and listener.
branches.cn: 没有障碍：清楚的语言就是说话者与听者之间的平地。

branches.en: NO COVER: direct speech says exactly what is meant.
branches.cn: 没有遮盖：直率的话说的就是本意。

branches.en: SHEER FACT: what is obvious needs no argument, so plain intensifies.
branches.cn: 纯粹的事实：显而易见的东西无需论证，于是 plain 变成强调词。

intro.en: Plain is a Latin loan that serves as noun, adjective and adverb; English built a small family of compounds around its two sense lines.
intro.cn: plain 是拉丁借词，可作名词、形容词与副词；英语围绕它的两条义线造出一个小型复合词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin planus 'flat' and its noun planities 'level ground' supply the base; explanare 'to make clear' is a related verb, which is why explain shares the root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 planus「平的」及其名词 planities「平地」提供基础；动词 explanare「使清楚」与之相关，因此 explain 同根。

items.example: The stem plan- carries both flatness and clarity.
items.exampleCN: 词干 plan- 同时带有「平」与「清楚」两层。

items.structure: Old French plain, from Latin planus
items.example: The plain lies open to the north.
Dust storms cross the plains in spring.
items.exampleCN: 春天沙尘暴掠过平原地区。

items.example: The plainest answer is usually best.
items.exampleCN: 最直白的回答通常最好。

items.example: The plainness of the room was deliberate.
items.exampleCN: 这个房间的朴素是刻意的。
一位直率的邻居提醒了我们。

items.meaning: flat land beside a river that floods
items.meaningCN: 河流旁边会被淹没的平地
items.example: The flood plain absorbs the spring melt.
items.exampleCN: 洪泛平原吸收春季融水。

items.meaning: to make clear, literally to make level
items.example: He explained the rule in one sentence.
items.exampleCN: 他用一句话解释了这个规则。

latinEntries.meaning: to make level; to make clear

definition_zh: 原告；起诉方；提出请求的一方
definition_en: the party who brings a civil case against another
core_image: 一叠写满委屈的纸被推过桌面，第一页最上面写着「我要求」，对面的人只看不接
