sceneCN: 这里 plaintiff 指在民事案件中提起诉讼、要求救济的一方（第 1 个义项：提起民事诉讼的一方）；句意：开庭前，这名原告在请求书中逐项列出了所有损失。图中可辨识物件：走廊长椅、赔偿清单、文件夹、法庭门。

pos.zh: 原告；起诉方（民事案件中提出请求的一方）

collocations.phrase: a plaintiff in a civil action

derivatives.zh: 诉苦；申诉（书面或旧式用法）
哀伤的；如泣诉的
哀伤地；如泣诉地

senses.title: The party who brings a civil case
senses.definition: the person or body that starts a civil action against another
senses.definitionCN: 对他人提起民事诉讼的个人或机构
senses.example: The plaintiff listed every loss in the claim before the hearing began.
senses.exampleCN: 开庭前，原告在请求书中逐项列出了所有损失。
senses.why: The word is built from the verb of complaining, so the party is named by the act of bringing a grievance before a court.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由「诉苦」的动词构成，所以这一方是按「把委屈带到法院」这个动作来命名的。

senses.title: The complaining party, literally
senses.definition: literally, the one who complains; the older force of the word
senses.definitionCN: 字面上指诉苦的人，这是这个词较早的力道
senses.example: In the old record the plaintiff is simply called the complainant.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧档案里，原告干脆就被称作「申诉人」。
senses.why: The French participle meant 'complaining', and the legal role grew out of that plain human act of stating a grievance.
senses.whyCN: 这个法语分词本意就是「诉苦的」，法律角色正是从「说出委屈」这一平常举动中长出来的。

senses.title: The party who files first
senses.definition: the party whose filing starts the clock of the case
senses.definitionCN: 其立案动作使案件时间开始走表的一方
senses.example: The plaintiff filed on Monday, and the summons went out on Tuesday.
senses.exampleCN: 原告周一立案，传票周二就发出去了。
senses.why: Procedure assigns the first move to one side, and that move is what makes the other side a defendant.
senses.whyCN: 程序把第一步分给一方，而正是这一步使另一方成为被告。

senses.title: The party seeking a remedy
senses.definition: the party asking the court for money, an order or another remedy
senses.definitionCN: 向法院请求金钱、命令或其他救济的一方
senses.example: As plaintiff, the tenant asked for the return of the deposit.
senses.exampleCN: 作为原告，租客要求返还押金。
senses.why: A case exists because someone wants something from the court, and the word marks that side of the demand.
senses.whyCN: 案件之所以存在，是因为有人想从法院得到什么，这个词就标记提出要求的那一侧。

senses.title: The first name in a case title
senses.titleCN: 案件名称中排在前面的当事方
senses.definition: in the style 'A v. B', the party named before the versus
senses.definitionCN: 在「甲诉乙」式名称中，排在「诉」之前的那一方
senses.example: The reporter read the case name with the plaintiff first.
senses.exampleCN: 记者念出案件名称时，原告排在首位。
senses.why: Court style fixes the order, and the first slot belongs to the one who brought the complaint, a rule still visible in case citations.
senses.whyCN: 法庭体例固定了顺序，第一格属于提出申诉的人，这一规则至今仍能在案件引证中看到。

senses.title: The party with the initial burden
senses.definition: the party who must first prove the basic elements of the claim
senses.definitionCN: 必须先证明请求基本要件的一方
senses.example: The plaintiff had to prove that the signature was genuine.
senses.exampleCN: 原告必须证明那个签名是真的。
senses.why: Whoever asserts must prove, so the procedural word also marks the side that carries the first load of evidence.
senses.whyCN: 谁主张谁举证，所以这个程序用语也标记首先承担证据重量的一侧。

senses.title: The party who starts arbitration
senses.definition: the party who brings a claim before an arbitrator or tribunal
senses.definitionCN: 向仲裁员或裁判庭提出请求的一方
senses.example: The plaintiff in the arbitration was a supplier from abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 仲裁中的原告是一家境外供应商。
senses.why: The same claim-and-answer structure appears outside court, and the label follows the claimant into private forums.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「请求—答辩」结构出现在法院之外，这个标签便随请求人进入私人裁判场合。

senses.title: An accuser in older usage
senses.definition: in older texts, anyone who publicly accuses another of wrongdoing
senses.definitionCN: 在较早文本中，指公开指控他人有错的人
senses.example: The pamphlet cast the widow as plaintiff against the guild.
senses.exampleCN: 那本小册子把这位寡妇写成了控告行会的原告。
senses.why: Before the word narrowed to civil procedure, it named any accuser, and historical writing still uses that wider reach.
senses.whyCN: 在这个词收窄为民事程序之前，它指任何指控者，历史文字仍保留这一较宽的范围。

intro.en: Plaintiff comes from Old French plaintif 'complaining', from plainte 'complaint', from Latin planctus 'lamentation', the noun of plangere 'to beat the breast'. The legal sense grew from the plain act of stating a grievance.
intro.cn: plaintiff 来自古法语 plaintif「诉苦的」，经 plainte「申诉」上溯拉丁 planctus「哀号」，即 plangere「捶胸」的名词。法律义从「说出委屈」这一平常动作中生长出来。

items.en: Plangere meant to beat or strike, especially the breast in grief, and so to lament. Its deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: plangere 意为击打，尤指悲伤时捶胸，因而意为哀号。其更深来源属来源不确定。

items.en: Planctus was the noun of that beating and wailing: a lamentation, a loud complaint. It supplies the stem seen in plaintive and plaint.
items.cn: planctus 是「捶打与号哭」的名词：哀号、高声诉苦。它提供了 plaintive 与 plaint 中可见的词干。

items.en: Plainte meant a complaint or lament in French, covering both the sound of grief and the formal statement of a grievance.
items.cn: 法语 plainte 指申诉或哀诉，既指悲伤的声音，也指正式提出的不满。

items.en: The adjective plaintif meant 'complaining', and it could stand as a noun for the person who complains, the exact shape English borrowed.
items.cn: 形容词 plaintif 意为「诉苦的」，可作名词指诉苦的人，英语借入的正是这个形态。

items.en: From the fourteenth century English used plaintiff for the party who brings a complaint to court, pairing it with defendant.
items.cn: 十四世纪起，英语用 plaintiff 指把申诉带到法院的一方，并与 defendant 配对使用。

items.en: The word narrowed to civil procedure, where it means the party who sues, while the older sense of any accuser survives only in historical prose.
items.cn: 这个词收窄为民事程序用语，指提起诉讼的一方；而「任何指控者」的旧义只留在历史叙述中。

note.en: Group one separates the complaint, the sad adjective, the unrelated look-alike and the related word with another prefix; group two sets the role against the other names for a claimant.
note.cn: 第一组区分申诉本身、表示哀伤的形容词、无关的形近词，以及带另一个前缀的同根词；第二组把这个角色与请求人的其他称呼作对照。

entries.definition: A complaint or lament, especially in literary or older legal prose; plaintiff is the person, not the text.
entries.definitionCN: 指申诉或哀诉，多见于文学或较早的法律文字；plaintiff 是人，不是文本。

entries.definition: Sounding sad or mournful; it describes a tone, never a party in a case.
entries.definitionCN: 听起来哀伤的；它描述语气，从不指案件中的一方。

entries.definition: Simple or flat, from Latin planus 'flat'. It resembles plaint but has no connection with complaining.
entries.definitionCN: 简单的、平坦的，来自拉丁 planus「平」。它形似 plaint，却与诉苦毫无关系。

entries.definition: A grievance or its formal statement, from the same wailing verb with a prefix meaning 'together'; it is not the party.
entries.definitionCN: 指不满或其正式陈述，同出「哀号」动词，前缀意为「共同」；它不是当事方。

entries.definition: The possessive form marking something belonging to the party, not a second role.
entries.definitionCN: 所有格形式，表示属于该当事方之物，不是第二个角色。

entries.definition: The party making a claim, common in tribunals and benefit cases; plaintiff is the standard court term in civil suits.
entries.definitionCN: 提出请求的一方，常用于裁判庭与福利案件；plaintiff 是民事法庭的标准用语。

entries.definition: The party who files a petition, as in divorce or family cases, where the word often replaces plaintiff.
entries.definitionCN: 提交呈请书的一方，如在离婚或家事案件中，常用它代替 plaintiff。

entries.definition: The person who makes a complaint, sometimes the victim or the reporting party rather than the suing party.
entries.definitionCN: 提出投诉的人，有时指受害人或者报案人，而不一定是起诉方。

entries.definition: Any party to a lawsuit; plaintiff names only the side that brings the claim.
entries.definitionCN: 诉讼中的任何一方；plaintiff 只指提出请求的那一侧。

entries.definition: The party who must answer the claim, the mirror image of the plaintiff.
entries.definitionCN: 必须对请求作答的一方，正是原告的镜像。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real verb of wailing, the real look-alike plain and the real court pair.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「哀号」动词、真实的形近词 plain，以及真实的法庭配对。

normal.en: Plangere is to beat the breast: the plaintiff is the one who brings the lament to court.
normal.cn: plangere 是捶胸：原告就是把哀诉带进法院的那个人。

normal.en: Plain means flat, not complaining: one letter alike, two unrelated origins.
normal.cn: plain 意为平坦，不是诉苦；字母相近，来源却全不相干。

normal.en: Plaint is the complaint, plaintiff is the person, plaintive is the tone.
normal.cn: plaint 是申诉，plaintiff 是人，plaintive 是语气。

normal.en: The pair is fixed: plaintiff and defendant, claim and answer.
normal.cn: 这组配对是固定的：原告与被告，请求与答辩。

normal.en: Whoever files first becomes the plaintiff and puts the other side in the answering seat.
normal.cn: 先立案的人成为原告，并把另一方放进应诉的位置。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of grievance sheets pushed across a desk, first line reading I demand.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠申诉纸被推过桌面，第一行写着「我要求」。

abstract.en: Picture a courtroom where the first name on the docket is the one who spoke first.
abstract.cn: 想象一间法庭，日程表上的第一个名字，正是最先开口的那个人。

abstract.en: Picture grief turned into a document: the wail becomes a claim with numbered paragraphs.
abstract.cn: 想象悲伤被做成一份文件：号哭变成分条列项的请求。

examples.en: The plaintiff asked for the deposit back and won.
examples.cn: 原告要求返还押金，并且胜诉。

examples.en: A plaintiff must prove the elements of the claim one by one.
examples.cn: 原告必须逐项证明请求的各个要件。

examples.en: The plaintiff and the defendant agreed to mediate before trial.
examples.cn: 原告与被告在开庭前同意调解。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑泪啼夫」——哭着捶胸、把委屈递上法庭的那个人 → 原告

root: 古法语 plaintif（诉苦的），源自 plainte（申诉），上溯拉丁 planctus（哀号），即 plangere（捶胸、哀哭）的名词。plangere 更深来源属来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the civil claimant, through the literal complainer, the first filer, the seeker of a remedy, the first name in a title, the initial burden, the arbitration claimant, and the older accuser.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从民事原告开始，经字面的诉苦者、先立案者、寻求救济者、案件名称的首位、先负举证责任者、仲裁请求人，最后到较早的控诉者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of grievance sheets pushed across a desk.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠申诉纸被推过桌面。

branches.en: THE ORIGIN: the legal party grows straight out of the plain act of complaining.
branches.cn: 来源：法律上的当事方直接由「诉苦」这一平常动作长成。

branches.en: THE FIRST MOVE: filing is what turns a grievance into a case.
branches.cn: 第一步：立案这个动作把委屈变成案件。

branches.en: THE DEMAND: the party is defined by what it asks the court to give.
branches.cn: 要求：这一方由它向法院请求什么来定义。

branches.en: THE PAPER AND THE PROOF: the first name in the title and the first load of evidence belong to the same side.
branches.cn: 文书与举证：名称的首位与第一批证据都属于同一侧。

branches.en: THE WIDER FORUMS: arbitration keeps the role, and older prose extends it to any accuser.
branches.cn: 更宽的场域：仲裁保留了这一角色，较早的文字则把它扩展到任何指控者。

intro.en: Plaintiff is a French adjective frozen into a legal noun, built on a Latin noun of wailing.
intro.cn: plaintiff 是一个冻结为法律名词的法语形容词，建立在拉丁「哀号」名词之上。

latinIntro.en: The base is plangere 'to beat the breast' and its noun planctus 'lamentation'; French added the adjective ending and English kept the whole shape.
latinIntro.cn: 基础是 plangere「捶胸」及其名词 planctus「哀号」；法语加上形容词词尾，英语把整个形态保留下来。

items.meaning: to beat, strike the breast, lament

items.meaningCN: 捶打；哀号（名词词尾把动作转成声音与事件）

items.example: The suffix made the participle an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把词干变成形容词。

items.meaningCN: 诉苦的（形容词化，随后可作名词）
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述诉苦的人。

items.structure: plaintif used as an English legal noun

申诉；哀诉（英语中缩短的形式）
哀伤的（形容词后缀把申诉转成语调）
items.example: A plaintive note ended the letter.
items.exampleCN: 信的结尾是一句哀伤的调子。

senses.title: The IAU definition
senses.titleCN: 天文学定义：绕恒星、近似球形、清空轨道
senses.definition: a body that orbits the sun or another star, is massive enough to be nearly round, and has cleared its neighbourhood of comparable bodies
senses.definitionCN: 绕太阳或其他恒星运行、质量足以近似球形，并已清空轨道附近同类天体的天体
senses.example: A single planet hangs in the eyepiece, striped and ringed.
senses.exampleCN: 目镜中悬着一颗有条纹、带环的行星。
senses.why: the definition was tightened in 2006 to separate planets from the many similar-sized bodies in belts, so three conditions replaced the older informal one.
senses.whyCN: 这一定义在 2006 年被收紧，以把行星与带中大量同样大小的天体区分开，于是三条条件取代了旧的松散说法。

senses.title: One of the eight
senses.definition: one of the eight bodies recognised in the solar system, from Mercury to Neptune
senses.definitionCN: 太阳系中公认的八颗天体之一，从水星到海王星
senses.example: Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system.
senses.exampleCN: 木星是太阳系中最大的行星。
senses.why: everyday use keeps the older, simpler list, so 'planet' usually means one of the eight even in careful speech.
senses.whyCN: 日常用法沿用更旧、更简单的名单，因此即使在谨慎的说法里，planet 通常也指八颗之一。

senses.title: A planet of another star
senses.titleCN: 其他恒星的行星（系外行星）
senses.definition: used with modifiers for bodies orbiting stars other than the sun
senses.definitionCN: 与修饰语连用，指绕太阳以外恒星运行的天体
senses.example: The telescope found a planet in a tight four-day orbit.
senses.exampleCN: 望远镜发现了一颗四天就绕一圈的行星。
senses.why: once other stars were known to have such bodies, the noun needed no new word; the modifier carries the difference.
senses.whyCN: 当其他恒星被确认拥有这类天体后，这个名词无需新词，差别由修饰语承担。

senses.title: Dwarf planet as a boundary case
senses.definition: used in the compound dwarf planet for a round body that has not cleared its neighbourhood, such as Pluto
senses.definitionCN: 用于复合词「矮行星」，指近似球形但未清空轨道附近的天体，如冥王星
senses.example: Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.
senses.exampleCN: 冥王星在 2006 年被改归为矮行星。
senses.why: the boundary had to be drawn somewhere, and the compound keeps the old word while marking the failed third condition.
senses.whyCN: 边界总得画在某处，而这个复合词保留了旧词，同时标出它未满足第三条条件。

senses.title: The earth as 'the planet'
senses.definition: used with the definite article to mean the earth, especially in environmental talk
senses.definitionCN: 带定冠词时指地球，尤用于环境话题
senses.example: We treat the planet as if its resources had no limit.
senses.exampleCN: 我们把这颗行星当作资源没有上限。
senses.why: seen from outside, the earth is simply one planet, so the definite noun becomes a way of speaking about all of us at once.
senses.whyCN: 从外面看，地球只是一颗行星，因此这个带冠词的名词成了一种把所有人一起谈论的说法。

senses.title: Living on another planet
senses.titleCN: 比喻：心不在焉、脱离现实
senses.definition: in the phrase on another planet, describing someone out of touch with present reality
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语「在另一颗行星上」，形容某人心不在焉、脱离现实
senses.example: His plan was elegant and completely on another planet.
senses.exampleCN: 他的方案很精巧，却完全不接地气。
senses.why: the image works because another planet is a place with different rules, so a person out of touch seems to live there.
senses.whyCN: 这个意象成立，是因为另一颗行星是一个规则不同的地方，脱离现实的人仿佛就住在那儿。

senses.title: Astrology's seven planets
senses.titleCN: 占星中的七行星（含日月）
senses.definition: in astrology, one of the seven traditional bodies: sun, moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn
senses.definitionCN: 占星中七颗传统天体之一：日、月、水星、金星、火星、木星与土星
senses.example: Old charts assign each planet a day of the week.
senses.exampleCN: 旧星盘为每颗行星分配一周中的一天。
senses.why: astrology preserves the ancient list in which the sun and moon also wandered, so its 'planets' are not the astronomer's.
senses.whyCN: 占星保留了太阳与月亮也会游走的古老名单，因此它的「行星」并非天文学家的行星。

senses.title: The old wandering stars
senses.definition: historically, any of the lights that moved against the fixed stars, including the sun and moon
senses.definitionCN: 历史上指任何相对于恒星移动的光点，包括太阳与月亮
senses.example: Ancient observers counted seven planets, sun and moon included.
senses.exampleCN: 古代观测者数出七颗行星，日月也在其中。
senses.why: the word meant 'wanderer' before it meant 'world', so the older list follows the original meaning rather than the modern one.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在指「世界」之前意为「漫游者」，因此旧的名单遵循原义而非今义。

senses.title: A world in fiction
senses.titleCN: 虚构作品中的「行星世界」
senses.definition: used in science fiction for a habitable or visited world with its own conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在科幻作品中指可居住或可造访、有自身条件的世界
senses.example: The crew landed on a planet where a day lasts a month.
senses.exampleCN: 船员降落在一颗一天长达一个月的行星上。
senses.why: stories need a unit of setting larger than a country and smaller than a galaxy, and the planet supplies exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 故事需要一个大于国家、小于星系的设定单位，而行星恰好提供了它。

intro.en: Planet comes from Greek planētēs 'wanderer', through Latin planeta and Old French. The word meant a moving star long before it meant a world. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: planet 来自希腊 planētēs「漫游者」，经拉丁 planeta 与古法语进入英语。在它指「世界」之前，很久以来都指会移动的星。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek astronomers called the five moving lights planētēs, 'wanderers', because they drifted against the fixed stars.
items.cn: 希腊天文学家把五个移动的光点称作 planētēs「漫游者」，因为它们相对恒星漂移。

items.en: Latin borrowed the noun as planeta and kept the meaning 'wandering star'; the sun and moon were often counted among them.
items.cn: 拉丁语借作 planeta，保留「游星」之义；太阳与月亮常被算在其中。

items.en: Old French planete carried the word into English in the Middle Ages, still as an astronomical body rather than a world.
items.cn: 古法语 planete 在中世纪把这个词带入英语，仍指天文天体而非一个世界。

items.en: From the seventeenth century telescopes showed planets as disks and worlds, and the word shifted from 'moving light' to 'physical body'.
items.cn: 从 17 世纪起，望远镜让行星显出圆盘与世界的模样，这个词便从「移动的光」转为「实体天体」。

items.en: The International Astronomical Union fixed three conditions in 2006 and created the dwarf planet category for bodies that fail the third.
items.cn: 国际天文学联合会在 2006 年定下三条条件，并为未满足第三条的天体设立「矮行星」类别。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Greek history of planasthai 'to wander' is not established, and any older Indo-European form proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：planasthai「漫游」在希腊语之前的历史没有定论，凡为其提出的更早印欧形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words derived from planet that name related bodies; group two holds sky objects that are often mistaken for planets.
note.cn: 第一组是由 planet 派生、指相关天体的词；第二组是常被误认作行星的天空对象。

entries.definition: The adjective of planet; it describes relations and systems rather than naming a body.
entries.definitionCN: planet 的形容词；描述关系与系统，而非命名天体。

entries.definition: A small body that looks like a planet but is not one; the -oid suffix marks resemblance, not membership.
entries.definitionCN: 形似行星而非行星的小天体；-oid 后缀标记相似而非归类。

entries.definition: One of the small bodies that collide and grow into planets; it is a stage, not a category of planet.
entries.definitionCN: 碰撞并长成行星的小天体之一；它是一个阶段，而非行星的一个类别。

entries.definition: Exo- 'outside' plus planet: a planet of a star other than the sun, so the head noun is still planet.
entries.definitionCN: exo-「在外」加 planet：太阳以外某颗恒星的行星，中心词仍是 planet。

entries.definition: A body that shines by its own fusion; planets only reflect light, which is why the two were once distinguished by motion.
entries.definitionCN: 靠自身核聚变发光的天体；行星只反射光，这正是两词最初靠运动来区分的原因。

entries.definition: A natural body orbiting a planet; a planet orbits a star, so the two words mark different centres.
entries.definitionCN: 绕行星运行的天然天体；行星绕恒星，因此两词标记不同的中心。

entries.definition: A place with its own conditions, often used for planets in fiction; it is a broader, older word.
entries.definitionCN: 有自身条件的地方，常用于虚构中的行星；是更宽、更古老的词。

entries.definition: The neutral word for any discrete object in space, used when the class is unknown or unimportant.
entries.definitionCN: 指太空中任何独立天体的中性词，用于类别未知或不重要时。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds, real relatives and real history, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的搭配、真实同族词与真实历史，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek planētēs 'wanderer': planets were the lights that wandered.
normal.cn: 希腊 planētēs「漫游者」：行星就是会漫游的光点。

normal.en: The family runs planet, planets, planetary, planetoid, planetesimal, exoplanet.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 planet、planets、planetary、planetoid、planetesimal、exoplanet。

normal.en: Three IAU conditions: orbit a star, be nearly round, clear the neighbourhood.
normal.cn: 国际天文学联合会三条条件：绕恒星、近似球形、清空轨道附近。

normal.en: The eight are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
normal.cn: 八颗是水星、金星、地球、火星、木星、土星、天王星、海王星。

normal.en: Astrology still counts sun and moon among its seven planets.
normal.cn: 占星仍把太阳与月亮算在它的七颗行星中。

abstract.en: Picture a marble circling a lamp in a dark room.
abstract.cn: 想象暗室里一颗弹珠绕着一盏灯转。

abstract.en: Picture a single room that must hold everyone's weather at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一个房间必须同时装下所有人的天气。

abstract.en: Picture a stranger who follows rules from a place nobody else can see.
abstract.cn: 想象一个按别人看不见的地方的规则行事的陌生人。

examples.en: Mercury is the smallest planet and the closest to the sun.
examples.cn: 水星是最小的行星，也是离太阳最近的一颗。

examples.en: Planets form from the same disk of dust that makes their star.
examples.cn: 行星由构成其恒星的同一片尘埃盘形成。

examples.en: The probe will study the planet's thin atmosphere from orbit.
examples.cn: 探测器将在轨道上研究这颗行星的稀薄大气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普拉内特（planet）」——天上到处乱跑的那颗球 → 行星

root: 希腊 planētēs「漫游者」← planasthai「漫游」，经拉丁 planeta、古法语 planete 进入英语；今义经望远镜观测由「移动的光」转为「实体世界」。planasthai 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses begin with the tightened definition, move to the eight, to other stars' planets and the dwarf boundary, then to the earth itself, a metaphor, astrology, the old list and fiction.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项先从收紧后的定义开始，再到八颗行星、别的恒星的行星与矮行星边界，然后到地球本身、一个比喻、占星、旧名单与虚构作品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one round body held in a path around a much larger light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个圆体被维持在一条绕更大光源的路径上。

branches.en: DEFINITION AND LIST: a strict rule and the familiar eight answer the same question at different depths.
branches.cn: 定义与名单：严格规则与熟悉的八颗在不同深度回答同一个问题。

branches.en: EDGES OF THE CLASS: other stars' planets and dwarf planets test where the word stops.
branches.cn: 类别的边缘：别恒星的行星与矮行星都在试探这个词的边界。

branches.en: ONE PLANET, TWO VIEWS: the earth as home, and a metaphor for being out of touch.
branches.cn: 一颗行星两种看法：作为家园的地球，以及脱离现实的比喻。

branches.en: OLD LISTS: astrology and ancient astronomy keep sun and moon inside the word.
branches.cn: 旧名单：占星与古代天文学把日月留在词内。

branches.en: STAGE OF A STORY: fiction uses the planet as its unit of setting.
branches.cn: 故事的舞台：虚构作品把行星当作设定单位。

intro.en: Planet is a Greek noun borrowed through Latin; English builds a large family from it with suffixes for relation, resemblance and size.
intro.cn: planet 是经拉丁借入的希腊名词；英语用表示关系、相似与大小的后缀从中构建了一个大词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin planeta and the adjective planetarius carry the word; Latin also said stella errans 'wandering star' for the same object.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 planeta 与形容词 planetarius 承载这个词；拉丁也用 stella errans「游星」指同一对象。

items.example: The Greek word named the moving lights.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊词命名了会移动的光点。
拉丁语保留了天文学义。

items.example: The planet has a four-day year.
items.exampleCN: 这颗行星的一年只有四天。

items.example: The eight planets differ greatly in size.
items.exampleCN: 八大行星大小差异极大。

items.example: Planetary science grew from telescope work.
items.exampleCN: 行星科学由望远镜工作发展而来。

items.example: The planetoid orbits between Mars and Jupiter.
items.exampleCN: 这个小行星体在火星与木星之间运行。

items.example: Planetesimals stuck together in the early disk.
items.exampleCN: 早期盘中星子粘合在一起。

items.example: Thousands of exoplanets are now known.
items.exampleCN: 现已知道数千颗系外行星。

stella errans (noun phrase, first declension + present participle)

definition_zh: 行星的；行星系统的；地球整体的；行星齿轮的

sceneCN: 这里 planetary 指「行星的」（第 1 个义项：与行星有关的）；句意为投影仪把一幅行星图像铺满整个穹顶。图中可辨识物件：穹顶、带环行星、环影、投影仪、座椅。

senses.title: Of a planet
senses.definition: relating to a planet as a body, its surface, interior or motion
senses.definitionCN: 指作为天体的行星及其表面、内部或运动
senses.example: A projector throws a planetary image across the whole dome.
senses.exampleCN: 投影仪把一幅行星图像铺满整个穹顶。
senses.why: the adjective was built from planet plus the Latin suffix -arius, so its base job is to attach 'planet' to another noun.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词由 planet 加拉丁后缀 -arius 构成，基本功能就是把「行星」挂到另一个名词上。

senses.title: Of a planetary system
senses.definition: relating to a system of planets and smaller bodies around a star
senses.definitionCN: 指围绕恒星的行星与小天体系统
senses.example: Planetary systems seem to be common in our galaxy.
senses.exampleCN: 行星系统在我们的星系中似乎很常见。
senses.why: once planets were known to come in systems, the adjective covered the whole arrangement rather than one body.
senses.whyCN: 当人们知道行星成系统出现后，这个形容词便覆盖整个布局，而不只一个天体。

senses.title: Planetary nebula, a misnomer
senses.titleCN: 行星状星云：一个历史误称
senses.definition: used in the fixed term planetary nebula for a shell of gas thrown off by a dying star, so named because it looked like a planet's disk
senses.definitionCN: 用于固定术语「行星状星云」，指垂死恒星抛出的气体壳，得名于它像行星的圆盘
senses.example: The Ring Nebula is a planetary nebula, not a planet at all.
senses.exampleCN: 环状星云是一个行星状星云，根本不是行星。
senses.why: early telescopes showed a round disk, so observers guessed 'planet'; the name stuck even after the object was understood as gas.
senses.whyCN: 早期望远镜只看到一个圆盘，观测者便猜是行星；即使后来弄清它是气体，名字仍留了下来。

senses.title: Planetary gears
senses.definition: used of a gear set in which smaller gears revolve around a central one, like planets around a sun
senses.definitionCN: 指小齿轮绕中央齿轮旋转的齿轮组，形似行星绕日
senses.example: A planetary gear set changes speed within a small housing.
senses.exampleCN: 行星齿轮组在很小的壳体内改变转速。
senses.why: engineers borrowed the astronomical picture because the motion is literally the same: several bodies circling one centre.
senses.whyCN: 工程师借用了天文学的图景，因为运动确实相同：几个体绕一个中心转。

senses.title: Planet-wide, as one system
senses.titleCN: 全球整体的、整个行星尺度的
senses.definition: relating to an entire planet treated as one system, especially the earth's climate and limits
senses.definitionCN: 把整个行星当作一个系统来看，尤指地球气候与其界限
senses.example: Climate change is a planetary problem that no single state can solve.
senses.exampleCN: 气候变化是一个任何单一国家都无法解决的行星级问题。
senses.why: earth science needed a word for processes that operate across the whole globe, and 'planetary' supplied it without adding a new root.
senses.whyCN: 地球科学需要一个词来描述遍及整个地球的过程，而 planetary 无需另造词根就提供了它。

senses.title: Astrological planetary hours
senses.definition: used in astrology for hours or rulers assigned to the seven traditional planets
senses.definitionCN: 占星中把时段或主宰者分配给七颗传统行星的用法
senses.example: Old almanacs listed a planetary ruler for each hour of the day.
senses.exampleCN: 旧历书为一天中的每个时辰列出主宰行星。
senses.why: astrology kept the older seven-planet scheme, so the adjective still carries a meaning that astronomy has dropped.
senses.whyCN: 占星保留了旧的七行星体系，因此这个形容词仍带有一层天文学已弃用的含义。

senses.title: Disciplines of planetary study
senses.titleCN: 行星研究各学科的用法
senses.definition: used in names of fields such as planetary geology, planetary atmospheres and planetary protection
senses.definitionCN: 用于行星地质学、行星大气、行星保护等学科名称
senses.example: Planetary geology compares volcanoes on earth and on Venus.
senses.exampleCN: 行星地质学比较地球与金星上的火山。
senses.why: each field studies the same class of object by a different method, so the adjective serves as the common label in their titles.
senses.whyCN: 各领域用不同方法研究同一类天体，因此这个形容词成为它们名称中的共同标签。

senses.title: Enormous, planet-sized
senses.definition: used loosely for something of enormous size or reach, as if it covered a planet
senses.definitionCN: 口语中形容某事物极其巨大或影响极广，仿佛覆盖整个行星
senses.example: The delay was a planetary embarrassment for the agency.
senses.exampleCN: 这次延误对该机构而言是一场行星级的难堪。
senses.why: the adjective can be exaggerated because a planet is a unit everyone can picture, so it works as hyperbole outside science.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词可以夸张使用，因为行星是人人都能想象的单位，于是它在科学之外成了夸张语。

intro.en: Planetary joins Greek planētēs 'wanderer', used of the moving stars, to the Latin adjective suffix -arius. The word first entered English through astrology and astronomy. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: planetary 由希腊 planētēs「漫游者」与拉丁形容词后缀 -arius 组合而成；planētēs 原指会移动的星。这个词最早经占星与天文进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek planētēs meant 'wanderer', from planasthai 'to wander'; the moving points of light were 'wandering stars' as opposed to fixed ones.
items.cn: 希腊 planētēs 意为「漫游者」，来自 planasthai「漫游」；会移动的光点被称为「游星」，以区别于恒星。

items.en: The verb planasthai 'to wander, roam' is the source of the noun; its own earlier history is not established.
items.cn: 动词 planasthai「漫游、游荡」是该名词的来源；它自身更早的历史尚未确定。

items.en: Latin took the Greek noun as planeta, still meaning a wandering star, and passed it to the European languages.
items.cn: 拉丁语把希腊名词借作 planeta，仍指游星，并把它传给欧洲各语言。

items.en: The suffix -arius formed adjectives of belonging, as in planetarius 'of the planets', also used for an astrologer.
items.cn: 后缀 -arius 构成表示归属的形容词，如 planetarius「行星的」，也用来指占星者。

items.en: English planetary appears in the seventeenth century as the telescope turned wandering lights into worlds.
items.cn: 英语 planetary 出现在 17 世纪，正值望远镜把游动的光点变成一个个世界。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): no exact first citation is firmly dated for the adjective, and the pre-Greek origin of planasthai remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：这个形容词没有确切可靠的最早书证；planasthai 在希腊语之前的来源亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same planet stem; group two holds adjectives of scale that overlap in use.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 planet 词干的词；第二组是用法上有重叠的尺度类形容词。

entries.definition: The body itself, from Greek 'wanderer'; the adjective adds relation, not a new object.
entries.definitionCN: 天体本身，来自希腊「漫游者」；形容词只是加上关系，不指新的对象。

entries.definition: A small body that accretes into planets; it shares the stem but adds -esimal 'small particle'.
entries.definitionCN: 聚合成行星的小天体；共享词干，加 -esimal「小颗粒」。

entries.definition: An asteroid-sized body, literally 'planet-shaped'; it is not a planet and takes a different suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 小行星大小的天体，字面「行星状的」；它不是行星，且用了不同后缀。

entries.definition: Inter- 'between' plus planetary: the space or travel between planets, not a property of one.
entries.definitionCN: inter-「之间」加 planetary：行星之间的空间或航行，而非某一颗行星的属性。

entries.definition: Covering the whole earth, from globe; it overlaps planetary in climate talk but names the earth only.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖整个地球，来自 globe；在气候话题中与 planetary 重叠，但只指地球。

entries.definition: Of the earth or its land, from Latin terra; it contrasts with planetary when planets other than earth are meant.
entries.definitionCN: 属于地球或陆地的，来自拉丁 terra；当指地球以外的行星时，它便与 planetary 相对。

entries.definition: Relating to an orbit rather than to the planet itself; planetary motion is described, but orbital names the track.
entries.definitionCN: 与轨道而非行星本身有关；行星运动会用到它，但它命名的是轨迹。

entries.definition: Belonging to the sky in general; planetary is one category within the celestial.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指属于天空；planetary 只是天空中的一类。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds, real relatives and real etymology, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的搭配、真实同族词与真实词源，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek planētēs 'wanderer': the planets were the stars that wandered.
normal.cn: 希腊 planētēs「漫游者」：行星就是会漫游的星。

normal.en: The family runs planet, planets, planetary, planetesimal, planetoid, interplanetary.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 planet、planets、planetary、planetesimal、planetoid、interplanetary。

normal.en: Fixed terms mark each field: planetary science, planetary nebula, planetary gear.
normal.cn: 固定术语标出各领域：行星科学、行星状星云、行星齿轮。

normal.en: Planetary nebula is a misnomer: it is gas, named for looking like a disk.
normal.cn: 行星状星云是误称：它是气体，得名于看起来像圆盘。

normal.en: Planetary gears copy the same motion: small wheels around a centre.
normal.cn: 行星齿轮复制同一运动：小轮绕中心转。

abstract.en: Picture seven bright dots that refuse to stay in their places.
abstract.cn: 想象七个不肯待在原位的亮点。

abstract.en: Picture a single round room containing every climate and every coast.
abstract.cn: 想象一个圆房间，装下所有气候与所有海岸。

abstract.en: Picture a small wheel circling a larger one inside a watch case.
abstract.cn: 想象表壳里一只小轮绕着大轮转。

examples.en: Planetary scientists compare the atmospheres of Venus and Mars.
examples.cn: 行星科学家比较金星与火星的大气。

examples.en: The planetary nebula glows because a dying star shed its outer layers.
examples.cn: 行星状星云发光，是因为一颗垂死恒星抛掉了外层。

examples.en: Water use has crossed a planetary boundary in several regions.
examples.cn: 在若干地区，用水已越过了行星边界。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普拉内（planet）」——天上那颗到处乱跑的星 → 行星的

root: 希腊 planētēs「漫游者」来自 planasthai「漫游」，经拉丁 planeta 进入欧洲语言；加拉丁后缀 -arius 成 planetarius，即英语 planetary。planasthai 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from one planet to a system of them, then to a misnamed gas shell and a gear set, then to the whole earth, to astrology, to named disciplines and finally to plain exaggeration.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一颗行星走到行星系统，再走到被误称的气体壳与齿轮组，然后到整个地球、占星、各学科名称，最后到纯粹的夸张。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a round body with a ring, standing for everything that circles a centre.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个带环的圆体，代表一切绕中心转的东西。

branches.en: BODY AND SET: one planet, then the arrangement it belongs to.
branches.cn: 天体与集合：先是一颗行星，再是它所属的布局。

branches.en: CIRCLING SHAPE: a gas shell and a gear train both borrow the round, orbiting look.
branches.cn: 环绕之形：气体壳与齿轮组都借用了圆形、绕行的外观。

branches.en: THE WHOLE AS ONE: earth processes and whole disciplines are named by the same adjective.
branches.cn: 整体为一：地球过程与整门学科都用同一个形容词命名。

branches.en: OLD SCHEME: astrology keeps the seven-planet meaning that astronomy dropped.
branches.cn: 旧体系：占星保留了天文学已弃用的七行星含义。

branches.en: BORROWED UNIT: a planet becomes a figure of speech for anything huge.
branches.cn: 借来的单位：行星成了形容任何巨大事物的修辞。

intro.en: Planetary is the noun planet plus the Latin suffix -arius; the stem also builds several scientific words with different suffixes.
intro.cn: planetary 是名词 planet 加拉丁后缀 -arius；同一词干还用不同后缀构成若干科学词。

latinIntro.en: Latin planeta 'wandering star' and planetarius 'of the planets' carry the Greek root into English; the suffix -arius also gives -ary in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 planeta「游星」与 planetarius「行星的」把希腊词根带入英语；后缀 -arius 在英语中作 -ary。

items.example: The root calls the planets wandering stars.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根把行星称作游星。

items.example: Mars is the fourth planet from the sun.
items.exampleCN: 火星是离太阳第四颗行星。

items.example: The outer planets are mostly gas.
items.exampleCN: 外行星主要由气体构成。

items.example: Ceres was once called a planetoid.
items.exampleCN: 谷神星曾被称为小行星体。

items.example: Interplanetary dust grains hit the probe.
items.exampleCN: 行星际尘埃颗粒撞上探测器。

items.example: The first exoplanet was found in nineteen ninety-five.
items.exampleCN: 第一颗系外行星于一九九五年被发现。

definition_zh: 浮游生物（随水漂流、不能自主逆流的微小动植物的总称）；浮游生物量
definition_en: the tiny plants and animals that drift in seas and lakes and cannot swim strongly enough to move against a current
core_image: 一滴海水在显微镜下被放大，圆形硅藻、带刺藻类与细小甲壳类悬浮在光柱里，随水缓慢旋转

senses.title: The drifting community as a whole
senses.definition: the whole assemblage of small aquatic organisms that drift with currents and cannot make headway against them
senses.definitionCN: 随水流漂移、无法逆流前进的微小水生生物的整体
senses.example: At night the plankton glowed blue along the hull whenever the oars stirred the water.
senses.exampleCN: 夜里，每当船桨搅动海水，浮游生物就沿船身泛出蓝光。
senses.why: the word is a collective mass noun, so it names the community rather than one creature; the Greek source means 'the wandering thing'.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是不可数集合名词，命名的是群落而非单个生物；其希腊语来源意为「漂泊之物」。

senses.title: Plant plankton that photosynthesises
senses.definition: the photosynthetic part of the plankton, mostly single-celled algae and diatoms, living near the sunlit surface
senses.definitionCN: 浮游生物中进行光合作用的部分，多为单细胞藻类与硅藻，生活在有阳光的表层
senses.example: Spring light lets phytoplankton double their numbers in a few days.
senses.exampleCN: 春季的光照使浮游植物在几天内数量翻倍。
senses.why: the collective splits by nutrition: plant-like drifters are phytoplankton, and the prefix phyto- 'plant' marks the class.
senses.whyCN: 这个集合按营养方式划分：类植物的漂流者即浮游植物，前缀 phyto-「植物」标出这一类。

senses.title: Animal plankton that grazes
senses.definition: the animal part of the plankton, from tiny crustaceans to jellyfish larvae, feeding on phytoplankton or on each other
senses.definitionCN: 浮游生物中的动物部分，从微小甲壳类到水母幼体，以浮游植物或彼此为食
senses.example: Zooplankton rise toward the surface at night and sink by day.
senses.exampleCN: 浮游动物夜间升向表层，白天则下沉。
senses.why: the prefix zoo- 'animal' marks the grazing half of the community, which migrates vertically with the light.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 zoo-「动物」标出群落中取食的那一半，它们随光照做垂直迁移。

senses.title: A local plankton assemblage
senses.titleCN: 某一水域的浮游生物群落
senses.definition: the particular set of plankton species present in one water body at one time
senses.definitionCN: 某一时刻、某一水域中实际存在的特定浮游生物物种组合
senses.example: The lake's plankton shifted from diatoms to green algae after the spring melt.
senses.exampleCN: 春雪融尽后，湖中的浮游生物由硅藻转为绿藻。
senses.why: ecology counts a community at a place and time, so the mass noun also serves as a countable unit of study.
senses.whyCN: 生态学按地点与时间统计群落，因此这个集合名词也可作为可数的研究单位。

senses.title: Biomass and sudden blooms
senses.definition: the total mass of plankton in a volume of water, or a rapid population increase visible as discoloured water
senses.definitionCN: 单位水体中浮游生物的总质量，或表现为水色改变的快速增殖
senses.example: A plankton bloom turned the bay green for three weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 一次浮游生物暴发使海湾变绿达三周之久。
senses.why: abundance is measured as mass, and when that mass grows fast it becomes an event with its own name.
senses.whyCN: 丰度以质量计量，而当质量快速增长时，它就成为一个有专名的事件。

senses.title: The base of the aquatic food chain
senses.definition: the first link of the pelagic food web, converting sunlight and nutrients into food for larger animals
senses.definitionCN: 远洋食物网的第一环，把阳光与养分转化为较大动物可食的物质
senses.example: Small fish filter plankton from the water and pass the energy upward.
senses.exampleCN: 小鱼从水中滤食浮游生物，把能量向上传递。
senses.why: from the organisms the word passes to their ecological role: whatever eats them begins a chain.
senses.whyCN: 由生物本身转向其生态角色：凡以它们为食者，都从这一环开始一条食物链。

senses.title: The biological carbon pump
senses.definition: the process by which plankton fix carbon near the surface and carry part of it to the deep sea as they die and sink
senses.definitionCN: 浮游生物在表层固定碳，并在死亡下沉时把其中一部分带到深海的过程
senses.example: Sinking plankton move carbon out of the surface layer for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 下沉的浮游生物把碳带离表层，一存就是几个世纪。
senses.why: the same drifting and sinking that defines the organisms becomes a planetary mechanism in climate science.
senses.whyCN: 界定这些生物的漂流与下沉，在气候科学中成为一套行星尺度的机制。

senses.title: Fossil plankton and ancient oceans
senses.titleCN: 化石浮游生物与古海洋
senses.definition: the mineral shells of plankton preserved in sediment, used to reconstruct past water temperatures and currents
senses.definitionCN: 保存在沉积物中的浮游生物矿质壳，用于重建古代水温与洋流
senses.example: Fossil plankton in the core place the ancient shoreline within the tropics.
senses.exampleCN: 岩芯中的化石浮游生物把古代海岸线定位在热带范围内。
senses.why: hard parts survive where soft bodies do not, so the community leaves a readable record in rock.
senses.whyCN: 硬壳在软体无法保存的地方留存下来，因此这个群落能在岩石中留下可读的记录。

intro.en: Plankton was coined in German as Plankton in 1887 by the marine biologist Victor Hensen, from Greek planktos 'wandering, drifting', the verbal adjective of plazesthai 'to wander'. English adopted it soon after. The word is wholly Greek and has no Latin cognate.
intro.cn: plankton 由海洋生物学家亨森于 1887 年以德语 Plankton 造出，源自希腊 planktos「漂泊的」——动词 plazesthai「漫游」的动词形容词。英语随后借入。该词纯属希腊来源，没有拉丁同族词。

items.en: Plazesthai meant 'to wander, roam, drift about'. Its deeper origin is uncertain, and not all the Greek verbal forms built on the same base are securely related; any Indo-European ancestor is a reconstruction.
items.cn: plazesthai 意为「漫游、徘徊、漂移不定」。其更深来源不确定，建于同一词基的希腊动词形式也并非都可靠同源；凡拟出的印欧语祖形均属重构形式。

items.en: Planktos is the verbal adjective 'wandering, drifting', formed from the same verb; it describes what is carried about rather than what moves itself.
items.cn: planktos 是由同一动词构成的动词形容词，意为「漂泊的、漂移的」；它描述被水流带着走的东西，而非自己移动的东西。

items.en: Victor Hensen introduced German Plankton in 1887 for the drifting community, contrasting it with nekton, the swimmers, and benthos, the bottom dwellers.
items.cn: 亨森于 1887 年提出德语 Plankton，指漂流生物群落，与自游的 nekton、底栖的 benthos 相对。

items.en: English borrowed plankton in the late nineteenth century; the exact first English citation is uncertain, but the term was established in marine science by the 1890s.
items.cn: 英语于 19 世纪末借入 plankton；最早的英语书证年代不确定，但到 19 世纪 90 年代该词已确立于海洋科学。

items.en: Phytoplankton and zooplankton were coined soon afterwards to separate the photosynthetic from the animal members, and bacterioplankton followed in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 此后不久便造出 phytoplankton 与 zooplankton，以区分光合成员与动物成员；bacterioplankton 于 20 世纪出现。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper root): Hensen's 1887 coinage is documented, but the pre-Greek origin of plazesthai is reconstructed, and the precise first English use is not fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词根）：亨森 1887 年的造词有文献可证，但 plazesthai 在希腊语之前的来源属重构，英语最早用例的确切年代亦无定论。

note.en: Group one separates plankton from look-alikes, including a Greek cousin in meaning and several unrelated words; group two places it among the other ecological categories of water life.
note.cn: 第一组把 plankton 与形近词分开，其中有一个意义上的希腊远亲，其余并无关系；第二组把它放进水中生物的其他生态类别中。

entries.definition: A flat length of timber, from Old French planche and Latin planca; the shared plank- string is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 指一块扁平的木板，来自古法语 planche 与拉丁 planca；共同的 plank- 字母串只是巧合。

entries.definition: Loud and mournful, from Latin plangere 'to strike, lament'; it resembles plankton in sound but comes from a Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指响亮而哀伤的，来自拉丁 plangere「击打、哀悼」；读音近似 plankton，但出自拉丁动词。

entries.definition: From Greek planetes 'wanderer', built on planasthai 'to wander'; it shares the notion of wandering with plankton, but the relation between the two Greek verbs is disputed and the referent is a heavenly body.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 planetes「漫游者」，建于 planasthai「漫游」；它与 plankton 共享「漂泊」这一意念，但两个希腊动词之间的关系有争议，且所指为天体。

entries.definition: The singular term for one planktonic organism, formed from plankton; it is a derivative, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 指单个浮游生物的术语，由 plankton 构成；它是派生词，并非另一词根。

entries.definition: The photosynthetic subset of plankton; it is a part of plankton, not a synonym for the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 浮游生物中行光合作用的子集；它是浮游生物的一部分，并非整体的同义词。

entries.definition: The animal subset of plankton, grazing on phytoplankton; again a part, not the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 浮游生物中的动物子集，以浮游植物为食；同样是部分而非整体。

entries.definition: Organisms that can swim against a current, such as fish; Hensen coined it as the opposite of plankton.
entries.definitionCN: 能逆流游泳的生物，如鱼类；亨森把它作为 plankton 的对立类别而造出。

entries.definition: Organisms living on or in the bottom sediment; it contrasts with plankton, which lives suspended in the water.
entries.definitionCN: 生活在底部沉积物表面或其中的生物；与悬浮在水中的浮游生物相对。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek planktos 'wandering' plus the noun ending -on: the wandering mass, named in 1887 by Hensen.
normal.cn: 希腊 planktos「漂泊」加名词词尾 -on：漂泊的一团，由亨森于 1887 年命名。

normal.en: Hensen's three categories: plankton drifts, nekton swims, benthos rests on the bottom.
normal.cn: 亨森的三分法：浮游生物漂流，自游生物游泳，底栖生物栖于水底。

normal.en: Compounds split the community: phytoplankton, zooplankton, bacterioplankton.
normal.cn: 复合词把群落分开：浮游植物、浮游动物、浮游细菌。

normal.en: The adjective is planktonic, the individual is a plankter, and the science is planktology.
normal.cn: 形容词是 planktonic，单个个体是 plankter，学科是 planktology。

normal.en: Plankton is a mass noun: ecologists treat it as a plural community, while 'planktons' is used only for separate types.
normal.cn: plankton 是集合名词：生态学者把它当作复数群体，而 planktons 只用于指不同类群。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd carried along a moving escalator, unable to walk back up.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人被移动的扶梯带着走，谁也没法逆着走回去。

abstract.en: Picture dust in a shaft of sunlight: each speck is tiny, but together they dim the room.
abstract.cn: 想象阳光柱里的尘埃：每一粒都极小，合起来却让屋子变暗。

abstract.en: Picture a slow snowfall in reverse, flakes rising to feed everything above them.
abstract.cn: 想象一场倒放的慢雪，雪片向上飘，供养上方的一切。

examples.en: Plankton form the base of the food web in both open ocean and lakes.
examples.cn: 无论在开阔大洋还是湖泊，浮游生物都构成食物网的基础。

examples.en: A sudden plankton bloom can deplete oxygen when it decays.
examples.cn: 突然暴发的浮游生物在腐烂时会耗尽水中的氧。

examples.en: Plankton shells in the sediment record past sea temperatures.
examples.cn: 沉积物中的浮游生物壳记录了过去的海洋温度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「plankton」读似「扑浪啃」——微小生物扑在浪上，随浪漂流啃食，正是浮游生物

root: 希腊 planktos「漂泊的」，为 plazesthai「漫游」的动词形容词；1887 年亨森造德语 Plankton，随后进入英语；纯希腊来源，无拉丁同族；plazesthai 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the community to its parts, then to its mass, its role in the food web, its carbon pump and its fossil record. The single image is a cloud of small bodies that goes where the water goes.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项由群落整体移向其组成部分，再到生物量、食物网中的角色、碳泵与化石记录。贯穿其中的意象只有一团微小躯体：水去哪里，它们就去哪里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cloud of tiny bodies suspended in water, moving only as the water moves.
core.cn: 核心意象：一团悬浮在水中的微小躯体，只随水的运动而运动。

branches.en: THE COLLECTIVE: the mass noun names a community, whether global or local.
branches.cn: 集合体：这个集合名词命名的是一群落，无论全球还是局部。

branches.en: TWO HALVES: plants that photosynthesise and animals that graze.
branches.cn: 两半：行光合作用的植物与取食的动物。

branches.en: MEASURED MASS: abundance becomes biomass and then a visible bloom.
branches.cn: 可测的质量：丰度化为生物量，再化为肉眼可见的藻华。

branches.en: PLANETARY ROLE: food for fish and a pump that sinks carbon.
branches.cn: 行星角色：既是鱼类的食物，又是把碳沉下去的一台泵。

branches.en: DURABLE TRACE: shells survive as fossils and record ancient water.
branches.cn: 耐久的痕迹：壳作为化石留存，记录古代的水况。

intro.en: Plankton is Greek throughout: the root plankt- 'drifting' plus the noun ending -on. English builds the adjectives with -ic, the individual with -er, and the science with -logy and -logist; compounds add Greek combining forms.
intro.cn: plankton 从头到尾都是希腊语：词根 plankt-「漂泊」加名词词尾 -on。英语用 -ic 构成形容词，用 -er 指单个个体，用 -logy 与 -logist 指学科与学者；复合词则加入希腊语构词成分。

latinIntro.en: Plankton has no Latin source and no Latin cognate. Latin-based terms such as suspension are only semantic equivalents, not relatives, so the list of Latin entries is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: plankton 没有拉丁语来源，也没有拉丁同族词。像 suspension（悬浮物）这样的拉丁系词只是语义对应，并非亲属，因此拉丁条目留空。

senses.title: A synthetic mouldable material
senses.definition: a light artificial material made from chemicals, used to make bottles, bags and countless objects
senses.definitionCN: 用化学原料制成的轻质人造材料，用来做瓶子、袋子等大量物品
senses.example: Most of the bottles in the fridge are made of plastic.
senses.exampleCN: 冰箱里大多数瓶子都是塑料做的。
senses.why: Greek plastikos described anything fit for moulding, so when chemists found a material that could be poured into a shape and set, the old word for mouldable was ready to name it.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 plastikos 指「适合被塑造的」，所以当化学家找到一种可以浇进模子再定型的材料时，这个古老的「可塑」之词正好拿来命名它。

senses.title: Made of plastic
senses.definition: made of plastic rather than metal, glass or wood

senses.example: She packed the sandwiches in a plastic box.
senses.exampleCN: 她把三明治装在一个塑料盒里。
senses.why: Once the noun named the material, the same form could stand in front of another noun as an adjective, simply marking what the thing is made of.
senses.whyCN: 名词一旦指认了这种材料，同一个词形就能站到另一个名词前面作形容词，只标示这件东西是用什么做的。

senses.title: Easily shaped or influenced
senses.definition: soft enough to be shaped, or figuratively easy to influence and change
senses.definitionCN: 软到可以被塑造，也可比喻容易受影响、被改变
senses.example: Young minds are plastic and quick to absorb new habits.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻的心智可塑性强，能很快吸收新习惯。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: the material sense grew out of it. Anything plastic takes an impression from outside and keeps it, which is why the word also describes a mind that can still be moulded.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，物质义正是从它长出来的。凡是可塑的东西都会留下外来的印记并保持住，所以这个词也能形容一颗仍可被塑造的心。

senses.title: Repairing the body by surgery
senses.definition: connected with surgery that repairs or reshapes damaged or unwanted parts of the body
senses.definitionCN: 与修复或重塑身体受损部位、不满意部位的外科手术有关
senses.example: The burn left a scar that plastic surgery could soften.

senses.why: Doctors who rebuilt damaged faces spoke of plastic surgery because they were literally reshaping tissue, borrowing the moulding image rather than the material one.
senses.whyCN: 重建受损面孔的医生把这类手术叫作整形外科，因为他们确实在重塑组织，用的是「塑造」的意象，而非「塑料」这种材料。

intro.en: Plastic comes from a Greek word for moulding, entered English through Latin and French, and only later became the name of a material.
intro.cn: plastic 出自希腊语中表示「塑造」的词，经拉丁语和法语进入英语，很久以后才成为某种材料的名字。

items.en: The verb plassein meant to mould clay or form a shape with the hands.
items.cn: 动词 plassein 意为捏塑黏土或用双手做出形状。

items.en: The adjective plastikos described what could be moulded, especially the art of the modeller.
items.cn: 形容词 plastikos 形容可以被塑造的东西，尤其指塑形这门手艺。

items.en: Latin took plasticus from Greek as a learned adjective; it is generally treated as a borrowing rather than a native Latin root.
items.cn: 一般认为拉丁语 plasticus 是从希腊语借来的学术形容词，而非拉丁本土词根。

items.en: French plastique carried both the moulding sense and, from the nineteenth century, the sense of a material that can be pressed into shape.
items.cn: 法语 plastique 既保留「塑造」义，也从十九世纪起指可以被压制成型的材料。

items.en: English plastic first meant mouldable, then named the cheap synthetic material of the twentieth century, and widened again to surgery and to flexible minds.
items.cn: 英语 plastic 先指「可塑的」，随后指二十世纪廉价的人造材料，又扩展到整形手术与灵活的心智。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Greek moulding stem and one near-spelling with a different origin; the near-meaning group gathers words for materials and for being shapeable.
note.cn: 形近组收希腊「塑造」词干上的词，以及一个拼写相近但来源不同的词；近义组收表示材料与可塑性的词。

entries.definition: The quality of being easily shaped or changed.
entries.definitionCN: 可塑性；易变性。

entries.definition: A soft coloured modelling clay sold for children.

entries.definition: A paste that hardens on walls; spelled alike but from Greek emplastron, not from plastikos.

entries.definition: Looking or feeling cheap and artificial, like plastic.

entries.definition: Made by chemical processes rather than found in nature.
entries.definitionCN: 经化学过程制成而非天然存在的；合成的。

entries.definition: Able to bend without breaking.
entries.definitionCN: 能弯曲而不折断的；柔韧的。

entries.definition: Easily pressed or hammered into a new shape.
entries.definitionCN: 容易被压打成型；有延展性的。

entries.definition: Created by people rather than occurring naturally.
entries.definitionCN: 由人造出而非自然形成的。

normalIntro.en: The word began as a comment on how easily something takes a shape, and that image still sits under the material, the adjective and the surgery.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词最初是在说某物多么容易被塑成形状，而这幅画面至今仍支撑着材料义、形容词义与手术义。

normal.en: Greek plassein means to mould, so plastic is literally the mouldable stuff.
normal.cn: 希腊语 plassein 意为捏塑，所以 plastic 字面就是「能被塑形的东西」。

normal.en: Plasticity keeps the old adjective stem and adds -ity, naming the quality itself.
normal.cn: plasticity 保留旧的形容词词干并加 -ity，直接指这种性质本身。

normal.en: A plastic bag is named for its material; a plastic smile is named for its fakeness, the same word pointing at two different judgments.
normal.cn: 塑料袋按材料命名，plastic smile 却按虚假命名，同一个词指向两种不同的判断。

normal.en: Plastic surgery reshapes tissue, so the moulding image survives even where no plastic is used.
normal.cn: 整形手术是在重塑组织，所以即便不用塑料，「塑造」的画面仍然在。

normal.en: Plaster looks close but comes from a different Greek word for a salve, so do not read it as a relative.
normal.cn: plaster 看着像，却出自另一个表示药膏的希腊词，不能当成同族词。

abstract.en: A material named after mouldability is a reminder that a word can describe a possibility before it describes a thing.
abstract.cn: 一种以「可塑性」命名的材料提醒人：词可以先描述一种可能性，再描述一件实物。

abstract.en: The same adjective covers a bottle and a smile, which shows how easily English lets a physical quality slide into a moral one.
abstract.cn: 同一个形容词既形容瓶子又形容笑容，说明英语很轻易就让物理性质滑向道德评价。

abstract.en: If something is plastic, it is not yet finished; the word quietly suggests that being shapeable is also being open.
abstract.cn: 说某物可塑，意味着它尚未定型；这个词悄悄暗示，能被塑造也意味着保持开放。

examples.en: The toy is made of brightly coloured plastic.
examples.cn: 这个玩具是用颜色鲜艳的塑料做的。

examples.en: Scientists are studying the flexibility and plasticity of the young brain.
examples.cn: 科学家正在研究幼年大脑的柔韧性与可塑性。

examples.en: Plastic waste is choking rivers in many countries.
examples.cn: 塑料垃圾正在堵塞许多国家的河流。

root: 希腊语 plassein（捏塑）→ plastikos（可塑的）→ 拉丁语 plasticus → 法语 plastique → 英语 plastic；一般认为拉丁形式是借自希腊语的学术词。

sensesIntro.en: The core is mouldability; from it come the material, the adjective of material, the old sense of being shapeable, and the surgical reshaping of the body.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「可塑性」；材料义、表材料的形容词义、古老的「可被塑造」义，以及重塑身体的手术义都由它长出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a warm soft lump pressed into any shape by the fingers, then cooling and holding that shape.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块温热的软料在指间被捏成任意形状，冷却后定型不变。
